name: Accordion
summary: Stacked sections that open and close. Each title is a heading holding the system Button that toggles its section. One or many open at a time.
useWhen: A long page of settings or answers where people need one or two sections at a time, such as an FAQ or account settings
A side panel that groups many controls into named sections that can be folded away
Content that is useful but secondary, where a short title says enough to decide whether to open it
avoidWhen: Content that most people need: hiding it costs a click for everyone
Switching between views of the same thing, where only one shows at a time and the choice should stay visible
Steps that must be done in order
A single section that shows or hides one detail

type.description: single: one section open at a time. multiple: any number open.

collapsible.description: With type single: the open section can be closed again, so all can be closed.

value.description: The open section, controlled: a string with type single (empty closes all), a list of strings with type multiple. Pair with onValueChange.

defaultValue.description: The section open at first: a string with type single, a list of strings with type multiple.

onValueChange.description: Called with the new value when a section opens or closes.

size.description: Trigger height and text size: sm is size.control.md (32px) with text s, md is size.control.lg (44px) with text m.

variant.description: data-variant. plain: no lines. divided: a border.default line under each section. card: each section on surface 2 with radius.panel and a gap.

headingLevel.description: The heading level, 2 to 6, that holds each trigger, so the sections fit the page outline.

disabled.description: On the root or an AccordionItem: the section cannot open or close. Its trigger keeps focus with aria-disabled and dims with opacity.disabled.

children.description: AccordionItem elements, each with one AccordionTrigger and one AccordionContent.

a11y.role: Each trigger is a native button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, inside a heading (level from headingLevel). Each open content is a region named by its trigger.
a11y.focus: Every trigger is in the tab order, disabled ones included (aria-disabled). The content's own controls follow their trigger. The trigger takes the Button's 2px focus ring.

keys.Tab: Moves to the next trigger, or into the open content
keys.Enter: Opens or closes the focused section
keys.Space: Opens or closes the focused section
keys.ArrowDown: Moves focus to the next trigger, from the last to the first
keys.ArrowUp: Moves focus to the previous trigger, from the first to the last
keys.Home: Moves focus to the first trigger
keys.End: Moves focus to the last trigger

a11y.announce: The trigger is announced as a button with its title and expanded or collapsed. The heading level lets screen reader users jump between sections.
notes: The order proposed an icon part. The trigger is the system Button, and a part inside it belongs to the Button, so the chevron is the Button's end content (data-part end), not an accordion part.
The chevron is the trigger Button's end content and is hidden from assistive tech; aria-expanded carries the state, the turn of the chevron shows it.
Arrow keys move up and down in both directions of text, as the sections stack.
Closed content is not in the page, so a search in the page does not find it.
Forced colors: the dividers and card edges become CanvasText lines; the trigger uses the Button's forced colors focus.
data-orientation is stamped by Radix on the root, items, headers and triggers, and is always vertical.

en.trigger: A noun that names the section, sentence case: Billing, Notifications. No question marks unless it is an FAQ.
en.content: Plain sentences. Say what the person can do here.

ar.trigger: Noun form, no diacritics: الفوترة، التنبيهات.

react.behavior: radix:Accordion, the trigger on the system Button through asChild
react.note: accordion-height: the content fades in and slides down space.xs as it opens (transform and opacity, duration.medium, ease.out), the chevron turns (transform). Closing is at once. Under reduced motion both are off.

angular.note: CDK accordion (cdkAccordion, cdkAccordionItem) with button[dsButton] as the trigger. Accordion.css as is.

native.note: rn-primitives accordion; the trigger is the native Button.

styles.studio: Ghost triggers on the page, a border.default line between sections in divided, surface 2 cards in card. The trigger hover is the 5% overlay.
styles.desk: The same, on Desk's surfaces and type. No recipe.
styles.neutral: Planned: no recipe expected.
styles.liquid: Planned: card sections stay solid content.

mistakes.wrong: Putting a button or a link inside the trigger
mistakes.right: Keep the trigger to its title; put actions in the content

mistakes.wrong: Tabs drawn as an accordion to switch views
mistakes.right: Tabs

mistakes.wrong: Every heading at level 3 inside a section that is already level 3
mistakes.right: Set headingLevel one below the heading that holds the accordion

mistakes.wrong: Hiding the one setting most people need inside a closed section
mistakes.right: Leave it open with defaultValue, or outside the accordion

name: Alert
summary: A message about the page or a section that stays until it is fixed or dismissed: a form error summary, a sync problem, a plan limit.
useWhen: A form failed to save and the person needs the list of fields to fix, placed above the form
A section cannot do its job right now: sync paused, a feed failed to load, a quota is near
A result that must stay readable while the person works on it, such as an import with skipped rows
A message tied to one place on the page, with up to two actions that fix it
avoidWhen: The message is about the whole app, such as maintenance or a trial that ends
The person only needs to know that something finished, and nothing is left to do
The person must decide before going on
Static guidance that is part of the content, such as a tip in docs
An error that belongs to one field

tone.description: The color, the icon and the tone word the icon says to assistive tech.

emphasis.description: soft is a tinted box, outline a tone border on the surface, solid a full tone fill. Keep solid for the one alert that matters most on a page.

size.description: sm for a dense panel or an inspector.

title.description: One line that names the problem or the result.

children.description: The body: what it means and what to do next. Text, paragraphs or a short list.

actions.description: Up to two Buttons, size sm, that fix the problem.

icon.description: A system icon name or a node in place of the tone icon. The tone word stays on the icon part.

toneLabel.description: The word the icon says. Default by tone and language: Notice, Information, Success, Warning, Error.

live.description: The alert is mounted after load and must be announced: role alert for danger, role status for the rest. Off for an alert that is on the page at load.

onClose.description: Renders the close button and is called by it. The consumer removes the alert.

closeLabel.description: The accessible name of the close button. Arabic under lang ar: إغلاق الرسالة.

a11y.role: No role when the alert is on the page at load. With live: role alert (assertive) for danger, role status (polite, atomic) for the other tones.
a11y.focus: The alert takes no focus. Tab reaches its actions, then the close button. When the close button removes the alert, the consumer moves focus to the next sensible place, usually the control that the alert was about.

keys.Tab: Moves to the next action, then the close button
keys.Enter: Runs the focused action or close button
keys.Space: Runs the focused action or close button

a11y.announce: Only with live. A role alert is read as soon as it mounts. A role status mounted with its text inside is not read by every screen reader (NVDA and JAWS can miss it), so for a polite message that must be heard, keep an empty live Alert mounted and fill it, or use a Toast. The icon is an image named with the tone word (Error, Warning), so the tone is read and never told by color alone.
notes: Mount a live alert when the problem appears. Do not set live on an alert that renders with the page, or it is read twice.
The close button is 24 by 24 px at every size (WCAG 2.5.8).
Native: accessibilityRole alert and accessibilityLiveRegion assertive only for a live danger alert; polite live region for the other live tones; none at load.

en.title: Name the problem or the result and the thing: Could not sync 3 files. Sentence case, no exclamation marks.
en.body: What it means and what to do next, in one or two sentences, or a list of the fields to fix.
en.actions: A verb plus a noun: Retry sync, Manage storage. Never OK, Continue, Confirm or Yes. Use Buttons of size sm in emphasis outline on a soft or outline alert: a soft Button on the tinted box can fall under 4.5:1. On a solid alert any Button takes the alert ink.
en.danger: Say what failed and what is safe: The server did not answer. Your local copies are safe.

ar.title: Name the problem in noun forms where you can: تعذر مزامنة 3 ملفات. No diacritics. Western digits.
ar.actions: Noun form labels, no diacritics: إعادة المزامنة، إدارة المساحة.
ar.lang: Under a Theme in Arabic the tone word and the close label switch to Arabic. Latin runs go through Bidi.

angular.note: The same DOM on Alert.css; the close part becomes CloseButton when it lands.

native.note: accessibilityLiveRegion assertive for a live danger alert, polite for the rest.

styles.studio: A flat tinted box with a faint tone edge, card radius, achromatic accent.
styles.desk: The same box on the desk surface; the accent tone takes the yellow primary.
styles.neutral: Planned: tokens only, no recipe.
styles.liquid: Planned: a solid box, never glass, since an alert is content.

mistakes.wrong: A red box with no icon or title word, only color
mistakes.right: tone danger: the icon says Error and the title names the problem

mistakes.wrong: live on an alert that renders with the page
mistakes.right: live only on an alert mounted after load

mistakes.wrong: An Alert pinned to the top for a maintenance window
mistakes.right: A Banner

mistakes.wrong: An Alert for Draft saved
mistakes.right: A Toast

mistakes.wrong: Three solid alerts stacked on one page
mistakes.right: One solid alert at most; soft for the rest, or one alert with a list

name: AspectRatio
summary: Keeps a box, and the image, video or embed inside it, at a fixed ratio of width to height at any width.
useWhen: A cover image, thumbnail or video that must not jump in height while it loads
An embed (a map or a video player) that should scale with its column
A grid of thumbnails that all share one ratio
avoidWhen: A single img or video you can style yourself: the native aspect-ratio CSS property on the element is simpler
Text content that must grow with its copy
An icon or avatar with a fixed size

ratio.description: Width divided by height, for example 16 / 9, 4 / 3, 1 or 3 / 4. A value that is not a positive finite number falls back to 16 / 9.

fit.description: How an img, video, iframe, picture or canvas child fills the box: cover crops, contain letterboxes. Sets data-fit. An inline svg fits through its own preserveAspectRatio.

asChild.description: Renders the single child element as the root through Radix Slot.

children.description: One media element, or any content that fills the box.

a11y.role: none of its own: a div. The media inside carries the name (alt text on img, a title track or label on video).
a11y.focus: Never focusable.
a11y.announce: Nothing.
notes: The ratio box reserves its height before media loads, so the page does not shift.
Content taller than the box is clipped. Never put text a person needs inside a ratio box.

en.alt: Alt text on the media says what it shows, in sentence case. Decorative media gets an empty alt.

ar.alt: Alt text in Arabic for Arabic pages, no diacritics.

react.note: Radix renders a wrapper div (data-radix-aspect-ratio-wrapper) around the root that takes 100% width; className, style and ref go to the inner root. No motion: nothing animates. Component CSS keeps that wrapper at align-self start, so a grid or flex row cannot stretch it out of ratio.

angular.behavior: [dsAspectRatio] directive on the native aspect-ratio property
angular.note: No Radix in Angular: the host sets aspect-ratio from the ratio input, so there is no wrapper div. The shared CSS styles the root and its media the same way.

native.note: React Native has aspectRatio on every view; fit maps to Image resizeMode cover or contain.

styles.studio: Layout only.
styles.desk: Layout only.
styles.neutral: Layout only.
styles.liquid: Layout only. Media stays solid under glass bars.

mistakes.wrong: An AspectRatio around one img that you style yourself
mistakes.right: aspect-ratio 16 / 9 on the img in your CSS, with object-fit cover

mistakes.wrong: A fixed height on a thumbnail so the grid lines up
mistakes.right: AspectRatio ratio 1 in each cell, which scales with the column

mistakes.wrong: A caption inside the ratio box
mistakes.right: The caption below the box, where it can wrap

name: Banner
summary: A page wide notice at the top of the app: maintenance, a trial that ends, an outage. A named region the consumer dismisses and remembers.
useWhen: A notice about the whole app or workspace: scheduled maintenance, an outage, a trial that ends
A condition that lasts across pages until it changes or the person dismisses it
One action that fixes the condition for everyone, such as Add payment method
avoidWhen: The message is about one section or one form
A passing confirmation of something the person just did
Marketing or a promotion that the person did not ask for
More than two banners at once

tone.description: The color, the icon and the tone word the icon says.

emphasis.description: soft is a tinted bar, solid a full tone fill for an outage or a blocking condition. Both are opaque.

children.description: The notice: one or two sentences, links allowed.

actions.description: Up to two Buttons, size sm. Use emphasis outline on a soft banner; on a solid banner any Button takes the banner ink.

label.description: The name of the region. Default Announcement, or Arabic under lang ar. Give each banner its own label when a page has two.

icon.description: A system icon name or a node in place of the tone icon. The tone word stays on the icon part.

toneLabel.description: The word the icon says. Default by tone and language.

sticky.description: Sticks to the top of its scroll container and sets that container's scroll-padding-block-start to its height (WCAG 2.4.11).

onDismiss.description: Renders the close button and is called by it after focus moves to the main content. The consumer removes the banner and remembers the choice; the banner stores nothing.

returnFocus.description: Where focus goes on dismiss: an element or a selector. A target that is not focusable gets tabindex -1.

closeLabel.description: The accessible name of the close button. Arabic under lang ar: إغلاق الإعلان.

a11y.role: region (a section with aria-label), so the notice is listed with the landmarks and can be reached from them.
a11y.focus: The banner takes no focus. Tab reaches its actions, then the close button. The close button moves focus to the start of the main content (the main element, or returnFocus) before onDismiss runs, so focus is never lost on the removed banner.

keys.Tab: Moves to the next action, then the close button
keys.Enter: Runs the focused action, or dismisses and moves focus to the main content
keys.Space: Runs the focused action, or dismisses and moves focus to the main content

a11y.announce: Never on its own: a banner is part of the page and is read with it. An outage that starts while the page is open is also told through a Toast or a live Alert. The icon is an image named with the tone word, so the tone is never told by color alone.
notes: A sticky banner reserves scroll padding for its own height on its scroll container, so a focused element is never hidden under it (WCAG 2.4.11). The previous value comes back when it unmounts.
The parts wrap at narrow widths: no sideways scroll at 320px (WCAG 1.4.10).
The close button is 24 by 24 px (WCAG 2.5.8).
One sticky banner per scroll container: two would overlap at the top and share one scroll padding. Stack a second banner without sticky under the first.
A sticky banner uses z.topbar and sticks at the top edge of its scroll container. Under an app top bar, put the banner in the content scroll container below the bar, not in the same one.

en.body: Say what is happening, to what, and until when: Scheduled maintenance on Friday from 22:00 to 23:00 Riyadh time. Sentence case, no exclamation marks.
en.actions: A verb plus a noun: Add payment method, Open status page. Never OK, Continue, Confirm or Yes.
en.label: Name the kind of notice when the page has more than one: Service status, Billing.

ar.body: White Saudi dialect or Gulf MSA, no diacritics, Western digits and 24 hour times: صيانة مجدولة يوم الجمعة من 22:00 إلى 23:00 بتوقيت الرياض.
ar.actions: Noun form labels: إضافة طريقة دفع، عرض صفحة الحالة.

angular.note: The same DOM on Banner.css; the scroll padding through a ResizeObserver in the directive.

native.note: Under the safe area at the top of the screen; the tone word in accessibilityLabel.

styles.studio: A full width opaque bar with a hairline on its block end; achromatic accent.
styles.desk: The same bar above the desk; the accent tone takes the yellow primary.
styles.neutral: Planned: tokens only, no recipe.
styles.liquid: Planned: a solid bar under the floating glass layer, never glass itself.

mistakes.wrong: A Banner for a form error
mistakes.right: An Alert above the form

mistakes.wrong: A Banner that stores its own dismissed flag in localStorage
mistakes.right: The consumer remembers the choice in onDismiss

mistakes.wrong: A sticky toolbar or banner that hides the focused field when tabbing
mistakes.right: sticky on the Banner, which reserves scroll padding for its height

mistakes.wrong: Three banners stacked at the top
mistakes.right: One banner, two at most, the most urgent first

name: Bento
summary: A grid of tiles of mixed sizes (1x1, 2x1, 1x2, 2x2) for overviews and landing sections. Reading order is the visual order.
useWhen: A dashboard overview with a few figures of different weight
A landing section that shows features as tiles of mixed sizes
Tiles where one or two deserve more room than the rest
avoidWhen: Every tile is the same size
Rows of records the user compares or sorts
The user rearranges or resizes the tiles
A long feed that loads more as it scrolls
Inside a narrow pane on a wide screen: the columns follow the viewport, not the pane

columns.description: Columns at full width. At most 2 under breakpoint.tablet, 1 under breakpoint.phone. React takes the numbers. Stamped as data-columns.

as.description: The root element. ul with items as li when the tiles are a list.

BentoItem.span.description: Columns by rows. Stamped as data-span. Every tile spans one column under breakpoint.phone.

BentoItem.as.description: The item element. li inside a ul root.

a11y.role: No role of its own: the native role of the element given by as. A ul root with li items is announced as a list with its count.
a11y.focus: Not focusable. Controls inside the tiles take focus in source order, which is the visual order.
a11y.announce: The tiles are read in source order. No dense packing, so a tile never moves ahead of one that comes before it in the source.

native.accessibilityRole: none, or list when the tiles are a list (root ul, items li)

notes: Reading order equals visual order: the grid flows by rows with no dense packing. A wide tile that does not fit leaves a hole rather than pulling a later tile forward.
One column under breakpoint.phone, so there is no sideways scroll at 320px.
In forced colors mode each tile draws an outline, since the fills are gone.
Under breakpoint.phone every tile is one cell: column and row spans reset.

en.item: A short label in sentence case, then the figure or the content. Figures use Western digits.

ar.item: Noun form labels, no diacritics, Western digits.

angular.note: Stamps the same data attributes; Bento.css is used as is.

native.behavior: A flex wrap of Views with widths from the span
native.note: One column on phones, so most native screens render a plain stack.

styles.studio: Tiles 1px apart on the body fill, square inner corners, the whole grid on the card radius (recipes/Bento.css). A hole left by a wide tile shows the body.
styles.desk: Free tiles on the black desk with a gap, each on the card radius.
styles.neutral: Free tiles with white space between them.
styles.liquid: Tiles are content: they stay solid, never glass.

mistakes.wrong: grid-auto-flow dense to fill the holes
mistakes.right: Order the tiles so they fit; dense packing breaks the reading order

mistakes.wrong: Placing a tile with grid-column-start to move it on screen
mistakes.right: Move it in the source, so screen readers and keyboard users meet it in the same place

mistakes.wrong: Every tile 2x2
mistakes.right: A Grid of equal tiles; Bento is for mixed sizes

mistakes.wrong: A ul root with div items
mistakes.right: as="li" on every BentoItem when the root is a ul

mistakes.wrong: Spans that leave a row part empty, so holes open in the grid
mistakes.right: Spans that fill each row; in Studio a hole shows the body next to square tile corners

mistakes.wrong: A focusable tile whose focus ring sits outside it
mistakes.right: An inset ring, since Studio clips the grid to its radius

name: Bidi
summary: Isolates each Latin run inside Arabic copy, so sentence punctuation stays at the logical end of the line.
useWhen: Arabic copy with a Latin term in it: a product name, a file name, a format such as JSON, a URL
A sentence that ends right after a Latin word and shows its period on the wrong side
avoidWhen: English copy: it comes back unchanged, so the wrapper adds nothing
Copy with markup inside: Bidi takes plain text only
A whole paragraph in another language: give its element a lang attribute

insteadUse.A paragraph in English inside an Arabic: an element with lang en, or a Theme with lang en to change direction too

a11y.focus: Never focusable. It adds no role.
notes: Each run is a bdi element with dir ltr. A run that opens with neutrals, like ~/.cursor, gets an explicit direction instead of a guess.
No invisible marks (RLM, LRM, U+202A to U+202E) are typed into strings: the markup sets the direction.

react.note: Lives in packages/react/src/theme/Bidi.tsx. The splitting is splitLatinRuns in @the-system/shared.

angular.note: A pipe or a component on splitLatinRuns from @the-system/shared.

native.note: Text runs with writingDirection from splitLatinRuns.

mistakes.wrong: Typing an LRM mark after a Latin word in an Arabic string
mistakes.right: <Bidi>{text}</Bidi>, which wraps the run in bdi

mistakes.wrong: Wrapping the period in the isolate with the Latin word
mistakes.right: Let Bidi find the run: it never takes trailing punctuation

name: Button
summary: An action the person takes on this page: save, send, open, delete. The one control that renders a native button.
useWhen: An action that changes data or starts a task on this page
The main action of a form, a dialog or a card, as tone accent with emphasis solid
A secondary or quiet action next to the main one, as soft, outline or ghost
A link that must look like an action, through asChild
avoidWhen: A control with only an icon and no visible label
Navigation inside running text
A choice that stays on or off
More than one solid accent button in the same view

insteadUse.A pressed or toggled state: ToggleButton (order 1.1.5). Until it lands, use a Button with aria-pressed and swap its emphasis between solid and ghost

size.description: Height from size.control: 24, 28, 32 and 44 px in the default density.

tone.description: The color family. accent is the primary action color of the active style.

emphasis.description: soft is the standard button of Studio and Desk (the source secondary). tone accent with emphasis solid is the primary action.

shape.description: default takes radius.control (Desk draws it as a pill), pill is fully round, square takes radius.sm.

loading.description: Shows the spinner and a visually hidden status (loadingLabel), sets aria-busy and data-loading, keeps the width and focus, blocks activation.

loadingLabel.description: What the hidden status says while loading, for example Saving changes or جار الحفظ.

disabled.description: Sets aria-disabled and data-disabled. Stays focusable so a Tooltip can say why. The native disabled attribute is never set. On an asChild link the href is removed while disabled.

start.description: Leading content: a system icon name or a node, before the label. Icons are 16px at every size, lg included, as in both sources.

end.description: Trailing content: a system icon name or a node, after the label. 16px at every size.

fullWidth.description: Fills the width of its container. Sets data-full-width.

wrap.description: Lets a long label wrap and the button grow in height. Off by default: the label ends in an ellipsis and the button shrinks with its row, so nothing scrolls sideways at 320px. Sets data-wrap. Desk draws no roll on a wrapping label.

asChild.description: Renders the single child element, for example a link, as the button.

type.description: Native type, so a button never submits a form by accident. Ignored with asChild.

a11y.role: button (native button element), or the role of the asChild element
a11y.focus: In the tab order in every state, disabled and loading included. A 2px ring on keyboard focus; every solid fill gets the doubled ring (focus.shadow.primary) so it reads against the fill.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the next control

a11y.announce: The label is the accessible name. While loading, a visually hidden status inside the button says loadingLabel (Loading by default) and aria-busy is set.
notes: Disabled and loading use aria-disabled, not the native disabled attribute, so focus never drops to the page when an action starts.

While disabled or loading, a click or middle click does not submit a form or follow an asChild link, and onClick, onAuxClick, onPointerDown and onKeyDown do not run. A disabled asChild link loses its href and keeps role link.
Icons inside the button are hidden from assistive tech. The label names the button.
Under forced colors the focus outline uses Highlight and the Desk roll is off.
No native title attribute. Hints come from Tooltip (wave 1).

en.label: A verb plus a noun in sentence case: Save changes, Delete project. Never OK, Continue, Confirm or Yes.
en.busy: Keep the label while loading. Say the verb in progress (Saving changes) in a live region, not on the button.
en.danger: Name what goes: Delete project, not Delete.

ar.label: Noun form labels, no diacritics: حفظ التغييرات، حذف المشروع. Never the imperative.

react.note: Motion: press, named from the pattern catalog that arrives in wave 1. Today: instant color swaps, the spinner, and the Desk roll label.

angular.note: The host element is the root. Inputs take the React prop names; start and end take an icon name or a TemplateRef. No asChild: a[dsButton] is the link form, and an inert link loses its href. Disabled and loading block click and auxclick with a capture listener. Button.css is used as is.

native.note: Styles from createButtonStyles(theme, variants) on the generated theme objects; Desk pill through packages/styles/desk/native/Button.ts. hitSlop reaches 44pt on iOS and 48dp on Android at every size. Press feedback: a Reanimated spring scale from spring.press, off under reduce motion. The Desk roll label is a web hover effect with no touch equivalent: not on native. No asChild and no token focus ring yet (the platform draws keyboard focus).

styles.studio: Bordered and filled overlay pills. The primary action is the neutral fill from color.primary (overlay 20 with the control border); the accent tint is the overlay too. Hover and press step the overlay at once.
styles.desk: Pill shaped at every size. The primary action is yellow #ffd84d with ink text and a doubled focus ring; accent soft is a yellow tint. The label rolls up on hover and keyboard focus, a copy rolling in from below (recipes/Button.css), off under reduced motion and forced colors and on a wrapping label.
styles.neutral: Planned: filled primary, outline secondary, 36 to 40px.
styles.liquid: Planned: capsule buttons with a press scale.

mistakes.wrong: Two solid accent buttons side by side
mistakes.right: One solid accent button for the main action, soft or ghost for the rest

mistakes.wrong: A button labelled OK or Continue
mistakes.right: A verb plus a noun that names the result: Save changes

mistakes.wrong: Swapping the label to Saving while loading
mistakes.right: loading on the button and the busy verb in a live region; the width holds

mistakes.wrong: A disabled button with no reason
mistakes.right: Leave it out, or keep it focusable and explain with a Tooltip

mistakes.wrong: An anchor styled with button classes
mistakes.right: Button with asChild around the anchor

mistakes.wrong: A Button with an icon and no visible text
mistakes.right: IconButton with a label

name: ButtonGroup
summary: A labelled row or column of two to five related actions, spaced apart or attached into one seamed control.
useWhen: Two to five actions on the same object that belong together: save, preview and share a page
A compact set of icon actions in a toolbar, attached: zoom in and zoom out, previous and next page
The actions of a form or a card footer, spaced, so they share one size and wrap together
The base of a split control: a main action joined to its menu trigger (SplitButton)
avoidWhen: Choosing one value or view from a set, where one option stays selected
Turning options on and off, alone or several at once
More than five actions, or actions that are rarely used
Actions that do not relate to each other, only placed near each other

insteadUse.More than five actions, or rare ones: DropdownMenu, or one main Button plus a DropdownMenu

aria-label.description: The group's name, for example Page actions. Required unless aria-labelledby is set.

aria-labelledby.description: The id of a visible heading that names the group. Required unless aria-label is set.

size.description: Passed to every child that does not set its own size. Spaced xs and sm groups use the smaller gap.

emphasis.description: Passed to every child that does not set its own. No default: each child keeps its own default (soft for Button, ghost for IconButton). No link: links are not grouped.

shape.description: Passed to every child that does not set its own. No default. Attached, only the outer corners take the shape.

orientation.description: A row or a column. Sets data-orientation. A spaced row wraps; a column stretches its children to the widest.

attached.description: Joins the children: no gap, inner corners square on the logical sides (they flip in RTL), a 1px divider. Sets data-attached. An attached row never wraps; its labels end in an ellipsis when squeezed.

fullWidth.description: Fills the width of its container; Buttons in a row share it equally, IconButtons keep their square. Sets data-full-width.

children.description: Two to five Buttons, IconButtons, ToggleButtons or SplitButtons. Tone stays per child.

a11y.role: group, named by aria-label or aria-labelledby
a11y.focus: No roving focus: every child is its own tab stop, disabled children included (they use aria-disabled). Attached children draw the focus ring inside their box, so the next child never covers it.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the next child, then out of the group
keys.Shift+Tab: Moves focus to the previous child

a11y.announce: Screen readers announce the group name when focus enters it, then each child by its own name.
notes: The group adds no keys. Arrow keys do nothing here; a set that should move with arrows is a Toolbar, a ToggleGroup or a SegmentedControl.
Every IconButton child needs its own label: the group name does not name its children.
Tone stays on each child, so a danger action in a group stays danger.
Under forced colors the system draws every child's border, so the seam stays visible, and the focus outline is pulled inside the child.

en.name: Name the group by what its actions act on: Page actions, Board view. Sentence case.
en.labels: Each Button is a verb plus a noun in sentence case: Save draft, Preview page. Never OK, Continue, Confirm or Yes.
en.order: The most used action first, in the reading direction. A destructive action last, or apart.

ar.name: Noun form, no diacritics: إجراءات الصفحة.
ar.labels: Noun form labels, no diacritics: حفظ المسودة، معاينة الصفحة. Never the imperative.
ar.order: The same order as English: it flips with the direction, so the first action sits on the right.

react.note: No motion: the group itself never moves; the children keep their own (Button press). The axes reach the children through ButtonGroupContext and, for direct children, as props they leave unset.

angular.behavior: [dsButtonGroup] host bindings, an injection token for the axes
angular.note: The host div is the root. Grouped dsButton directives read the axes from the token and let their own inputs win. ButtonGroup.css is used as is.

native.behavior: react-native:View with accessibilityRole none and an accessibilityLabel
native.note: Attached corners through the style function, flipped by I18nManager.

styles.studio: Overlay filled children. Attached, the seam is color.border.default over the overlay fill; the control radius rounds only the outer corners.
styles.desk: Children are pills, so an attached group reads as one pill with square inner corners. The roll label runs in each child as usual.
styles.neutral: Takes the tokens of the Neutral style, no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: A ButtonGroup with one button marked as the selected view
mistakes.right: SegmentedControl, which keeps one option selected and says so

mistakes.wrong: Eight actions in one attached group
mistakes.right: At most five; the rest in a DropdownMenu behind a More actions IconButton

mistakes.wrong: A group with no aria-label or aria-labelledby
mistakes.right: A name that says what the actions act on: Page actions

mistakes.wrong: Two solid accent buttons attached side by side as two main actions
mistakes.right: One main action, or a SplitButton for a main action with variants

mistakes.wrong: An attached group of Buttons and IconButtons with no emphasis, so soft Buttons sit next to a ghost IconButton
mistakes.right: Set emphasis on the attached group, so every child shares one fill

mistakes.wrong: Arrow keys wired to move between the children
mistakes.right: Leave each child in the tab order, or use Toolbar for arrow key navigation

name: Callout
summary: A static note inside content: a tip, a caution or a fact to keep in mind, read in reading order with the text around it.
useWhen: A tip or a caution inside docs, help or a settings page
A fact a reader should not miss before a step, such as Deleting a team deletes its boards
Side guidance next to a form that is true whatever the person does
A short list of steps set apart from running text
avoidWhen: The message is about a problem that appeared after load and must be announced
The message is about the whole app
The person must act on it before going on
The note holds actions or a close button

tone.description: The color, the icon and the tone word: Note, Tip, Information, Success, Warning, Caution.

emphasis.description: soft is a tinted box, outline a tone border on the surface. Both keep the strong tone edge on the inline start side.

title.description: A short line that sums up the note. Optional: without it the tone word names the callout.

children.description: The note: text, paragraphs, a list, links or inline code.

icon.description: A system icon name or a node in place of the tone icon. The tone word stays on the icon part.

toneLabel.description: The word the icon says and the start of the callout's name. Default by tone and language.

as.description: div renders role note inside running content. aside renders a complementary landmark, for a note beside the main content; keep it outside other landmarks.

a11y.role: note (a div), or complementary (an aside). Named by the tone word on the icon and the title through aria-labelledby, for example Tip Move faster with the keyboard. An aria-label or aria-labelledby from the consumer wins.
a11y.focus: None. The callout takes no focus; links inside it are in the normal tab order.
a11y.announce: Never. No live role: it is read in reading order with the content around it. The icon is an image named with the tone word, so the tone is never told by color alone.
notes: No motion: a callout never moves, so it needs no reduced motion form.
No actions or close part: a note the person can dismiss or act on is an Alert.

en.title: A short line that sums up the note: Works offline. Sentence case, no exclamation marks.
en.body: One or two sentences, or a short list. Name the mechanism: Press the slash key to search.
en.danger: Say what is lost and how to avoid it: Deleting a team deletes its boards. Move them first.

ar.title: Noun forms where you can: العمل بدون اتصال. No diacritics. Western digits.
ar.lang: Under a Theme in Arabic the tone word switches to Arabic. Latin runs and code go through Bidi.

angular.note: The same DOM on Callout.css, ids from the CDK id generator.

native.note: A View with accessibilityRole text and the tone word at the start of its accessibilityLabel.

styles.studio: A tinted box with small corners and a 2px tone edge on the inline start side; achromatic accent.
styles.desk: The same box; the accent tone takes the yellow primary edge.
styles.neutral: Planned: tokens only, no recipe.
styles.liquid: Planned: a solid box, never glass, since a callout is content.

mistakes.wrong: A Callout for a sync error that appeared after load
mistakes.right: An Alert with live, so it is announced

mistakes.wrong: A Callout with a Retry button and a close button
mistakes.right: An Alert, which has actions and close

mistakes.wrong: Every paragraph of a page in a callout
mistakes.right: One callout per section at most; the rest is plain text

mistakes.wrong: as aside inside main content where it is not tangential
mistakes.right: The default div with role note

name: Card
summary: A bordered, filled or raised container for one item: optional media, a header with a title and a description, a body, and a footer with actions. The whole card can be one link.
useWhen: One item among several that each need a title, a short summary and an action, such as a board, a project or a plan
A whole card that opens a detail page, through one CardLink in the title
A group of related settings or figures that reads as one block on a page
avoidWhen: A dense grid of files or boards in Studio, where tiles split by a 1px gap read better
Rows that people scan and compare, such as a list of messages or a table
A choice of one option out of several
Wrapping a whole page section only to draw a border around it

emphasis.description: outline: a hairline border on the surface. soft: one tone step up, no border. solid: the tone step plus elevation.menu, a soft drop shadow in both Studio and Desk, which steps to elevation.panel on hover.

size.description: Padding and the gap between parts: space l, 2xl and 4xl. sm takes radius.panel, md and lg take radius.card.

selected.description: Draws a 2px ring inside the border (not color alone) and sets data-selected. Say it in words too: aria-current on the CardLink or a checkbox in the card.

disabled.description: Sets data-disabled, mutes the title, dims the media with opacity.disabled and removes the CardLink href (aria-disabled, role link). Text stays at 4.5:1: a card is not a control, so the contrast exception does not cover it. Actions are disabled by the caller.

asChild.description: Renders the single child element as the root, for example an li inside a ul of cards or an article.

level.description: On CardTitle: the heading level, so the card fits the outline of its page.

href.description: On CardLink: the link target. Its hit area covers the whole card.

children.description: The parts: CardMedia, CardHeader (CardTitle, CardDescription), CardBody, CardFooter (CardActions).

a11y.role: None on the root (a div, or the asChild element). The title is a heading. A whole card link is one native link inside the title.
a11y.focus: The card itself never takes focus. Tab reaches the CardLink, then each action. While the link has keyboard focus the whole card shows the 2px ring from focus.shadow.ring.

keys.Tab: Moves to the card link, then to each action in the footer
keys.Enter: On the card link: opens it

a11y.announce: The link is named by the title text. Description and body are read in order after it. Selection is announced through aria-current on the link or a checkbox, which the caller sets.
notes: A whole card link is one real link and a stretched target (the link's ::before covers the card). Never wrap the card in a link and never put a button inside the link.

Actions sit above the stretched target, so they keep their own 24px targets and do not open the link. Interactive content goes in CardActions only: a link or button in the body sits under the target and cannot be clicked.
A disabled CardLink keeps tabIndex 0 and aria-disabled, so it stays in the tab order (convention 5); a click does nothing.
Text under the stretched target cannot be selected with the pointer. Keep long text that people copy out of an interactive card.
Forced colors: the border becomes CanvasText, the selected card gets a Highlight outline inside its border and focus shows as a Highlight outline.

en.title: The item's name, sentence case, no end period: Spring launch.
en.description: One line of context: Updated 2 hours ago, 4 boards.
en.actions: A verb plus a noun: Share board. An icon only action names its item: More actions for Spring launch.

ar.title: The item's name in white Saudi dialect, no diacritics: إطلاق الربيع.
ar.description: Short and plain, Western digits: آخر تحديث قبل 3 أيام.

react.note: Motion: an interactive card rises by space.4xs on hover (transform only) and its hover veil fades in (opacity), off under reduced motion. Named fade-rise from the 1.11 catalog list; no catalog pattern covers a hover lift yet.

angular.note: dsCard on the host, parts as attribute directives (dsCardTitle, a[dsCardLink]). Card.css as is.

native.note: A View with the same parts. A whole card link is a Pressable root with the title as its label; actions as separate Pressables beside it.

styles.studio: outline is the surface with the default border, soft is the surface 2 tone step. solid adds Studio's menu shadow (12 by 28px). An interactive card rises by space.4xs on hover, takes elevation.card-hover (a soft two layer shadow) and a 5% veil; soft and solid also step to surface 3.
styles.desk: The same parts on the Desk surfaces; solid takes the Desk menu shadow and the panel shadow on hover.
styles.neutral: Planned: small soft shadows and 1px borders from Neutral's tokens, no recipe expected.
styles.liquid: Planned: cards stay solid content under the glass layer.

mistakes.wrong: Wrapping the whole card in an anchor with buttons inside it
mistakes.right: One CardLink inside CardTitle; buttons in CardActions sit above its stretched target

mistakes.wrong: Showing selection only with a border color
mistakes.right: selected draws a 2px ring, and aria-current or a checkbox says it in words

mistakes.wrong: A Studio file grid of outlined cards with gaps
mistakes.right: Tile inside TileGrid, split by the 1px gap

mistakes.wrong: An action labelled More with no item name
mistakes.right: More actions for Spring launch

name: Container
summary: Centers page content at a max width with a gutter on both inline sides.
useWhen: The content column of a page or a landing section, centered on wide screens
Capping the line length of reading text at a narrow width
Keeping the 16px phone gutter on any page content
avoidWhen: Inside a panel, card or dialog that already has its own padding
Laying out children in a row or columns
A full bleed band of color or media that must reach the screen edges

width.description: The max inline size, gutter included: sm 30rem (breakpoint.phone), md 48rem (breakpoint.tablet), lg 68.75rem (breakpoint.desktop), xl desktop plus half a phone (about 84rem), full no cap. Named width, not size, because size is the shared control axis. Sets data-width.

gutter.description: Padding on both inline sides, a space.* step. 3xl is 16px on phones in the default density. Sets data-gutter.

as.description: The element to render. One main per page.

a11y.role: none of its own: a div, or the landmark of as
a11y.focus: Never focusable.
a11y.announce: Nothing. A Container is layout only.
notes: Content never scrolls sideways at 320px: the width is a max, the box is 100% and the gutter sits inside it (WCAG 1.4.10).
Width sm keeps reading text near 70 characters a line.

ar.body: No copy of its own. The gutter is the same on both sides, so nothing changes in Arabic.

react.note: No motion: a static layout has nothing to animate, so no pattern from the catalog applies.

angular.note: The host element is the root, so as is not needed.

native.behavior: react-native:View with maxWidth, alignSelf center and paddingHorizontal
native.note: Respect the safe area insets on top of the gutter.

styles.studio: Layout only.
styles.desk: Layout only. Pages sit inside windows, so a Container is mostly for site pages.
styles.neutral: Layout only.
styles.liquid: Layout only. Content scrolls under the glass bars; the gutter stays.

mistakes.wrong: A Container inside a Dialog body or a Card
mistakes.right: No Container: the panel already pads its content

mistakes.wrong: max-width 1200px and padding 0 16px written by hand
mistakes.right: Container width lg, which keeps the gutter and the logical margins

mistakes.wrong: size xl to pick a page width
mistakes.right: width xl; size is the control size axis

mistakes.wrong: Two Containers rendered as main on one page
mistakes.right: One main per page; the rest as div or section

name: DescriptionList
summary: Term and value pairs on a dl: the details of an order, a summary of settings, the facts about a record.
useWhen: Read only facts about one thing: order number, date, payment, total
A summary of settings before people confirm or edit them
Metadata in a side panel or a card: owner, created on, size
avoidWhen: Values people edit in place
Many records with the same fields, compared row by row
A single headline number
A list of rows people open or act on

insteadUse.Values people edit: Field with the matching control, in a form

orientation.description: horizontal: terms in a column at the start, values beside them; the column takes the longest term up to 40 percent and every item stacks under breakpoint.phone. vertical: each term above its value. Sets data-orientation.

size.description: Text size font.size s or m, with the gaps to match.

items.description: The pairs as data: an array of { key?, term, details }, where details is one node or an array of nodes (one dd each). Rendered before children.

children.description: DescriptionListItem elements: term, and the value as children or several values as details (each in its own dd).

a11y.role: None beyond the native dl, dt and dd. Each pair sits in a div, which HTML allows inside dl.
a11y.focus: Never focusable itself. Links or buttons inside a value keep their own focus.
a11y.announce: Screen readers read each term with its value. Some also say it is a list.
notes: Terms are nouns without a colon; the layout shows the pairing.
Values wrap anywhere, so a long URL or a long Arabic address never scrolls sideways at 320px.
Terms are muted text; check that a recipe keeps 4.5:1 on the surface the list sits on.
Latin codes inside Arabic values (order numbers, URLs) go through Bidi.
The stack under breakpoint.phone follows the viewport, not the list width; use vertical in a narrow panel.

en.term: A noun in sentence case, no colon: Order number, Delivery address.
en.details: The value as people read it: dates in words, amounts with the currency. An unset value says Not set.

ar.term: Noun form, no diacritics, no colon: رقم الطلب، عنوان التوصيل.
ar.details: Western digits. Latin codes such as GB-20481 stay left to right inside the value.

native.note: Rows of Text with the same props; no dl on native, so the role is text and pairs are read in order.

styles.studio: Muted terms, default text values, compact gaps.
styles.desk: The same on the Desk tokens in Instrument Sans.
styles.neutral: The same on the Neutral tokens; no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: Terms written as Order number: with a colon
mistakes.right: Order number; the columns pair the term and the value

mistakes.wrong: A table of two columns for one record's details
mistakes.right: DescriptionList, which screen readers read as pairs

mistakes.wrong: Inputs inside details to edit values in place
mistakes.right: A form with Field, or an edit button that opens one

mistakes.wrong: An empty dd for a missing value
mistakes.right: Not set, or leave the pair out

name: Dialog
summary: A modal task that must be finished or dismissed. The page behind it is covered by a backdrop, hidden from assistive tech and out of reach until the dialog closes.
useWhen: A decision blocks the rest of the page
A short form of up to five fields
A destructive action that needs one more look before it runs
avoidWhen: Long content, or content compared with the page
A message that needs no decision
Work the person does next to the page, moving between both
An action that cannot be undone and must not be dismissed by accident

onOpenChange.description: Called with false for Escape, a backdrop click, the close control and DialogClose.

size.description: The width from the dialog.width tokens: 360, 440, 520, 640 and 820 px, never wider than the viewport minus a gutter.

tone.description: danger: a destructive decision. The title takes the danger color and focus opens on the Cancel action.

dismissible.description: false: only the dialog's own actions close it. Escape and a backdrop click do nothing and the close control is disabled (aria-disabled). For short waits while an action runs: the app sets it back to true when the action ends.

title.description: DialogContent: the title for the common case, the same as a DialogTitle as its first child.

description.description: DialogContent: the description for the common case.

closeLabel.description: DialogContent: the accessible name of the close control. Arabic default under lang ar: إغلاق النافذة.

controlsLabel.description: DialogContent: the accessible name of the Desk lights group.

rootProps.description: DialogContent: props for the root layer. className and style go to the root too; ref and every other prop go to the panel, the element with role dialog, Radix Content props included. The useful ones: onOpenAutoFocus (preventDefault to place focus yourself), onCloseAutoFocus (preventDefault and focus another element when the trigger is gone, for example after a delete), onEscapeKeyDown (preventDefault to keep the dialog open, for example while a field holds unsaved text).

DialogTrigger.description: One child element, a system Button, rendered as the trigger (always asChild). It opens the dialog, gets aria-haspopup, aria-expanded and aria-controls, and takes focus back on close.

DialogClose.description: One child element, a system Button, that closes the dialog (always asChild). It is marked data-dialog-cancel: in a danger dialog focus opens on it. Wrap only the Cancel action.

data-autofocus.description: Put on any focusable element inside the dialog to take focus on open, before every other rule of the focus rule.

a11y.role: dialog (the panel), modal: Radix hides the rest of the page from assistive tech and keeps focus inside. Named by the title (aria-labelledby), described by the description (aria-describedby).
a11y.focus: On open, focus goes to an element marked data-autofocus; else to the first field in the body; else to the first footer action that is not tone danger; when tone is danger, to the Cancel action (the DialogClose) or else the first footer action that is not tone danger, never a destructive one; else to the close control. On close, focus returns to the trigger, or to the element that had focus before the dialog opened; when that element is gone, to its nearest connected focusable ancestor, else the first tab stop of main, else the body.

keys.Escape: Closes the dialog, unless dismissible is false. Escape from inside the dialog closes the dialog even while a toast shows above it. A nested dialog or a menu on top closes first.
keys.Tab: Moves to the next control inside the dialog and wraps from the last to the first
keys.Shift+Tab: Moves to the previous control inside the dialog and wraps from the first to the last

a11y.announce: The title and the description are read when the dialog opens. The close control and the Desk lights carry their own labels.
notes: role dialog in every tone. A danger dialog stays a dialog: AlertDialog arrives in wave 1 for actions that cannot be undone.
The page behind does not scroll while the dialog is open (Radix scroll lock); pinch zoom stays on.
A body taller than dialog.height-max scrolls inside, and joins the tab order while it scrolls so the keyboard can scroll it. The title and the footer stay in view.
A click on the backdrop closes the dialog, unless dismissible is false. The close control is the button path for the same action.

Toasts sit above an open dialog (z.toast over z.dialog): they stay visible, their live region is not hidden from screen readers, and a pointer click on a toast action or close button works without closing the dialog. Keyboard focus stays in the dialog: F8 and Tab do not reach the toasts (DECISIONS.md, Components 1). Toasts with an action or the danger tone never time out, so they are still there when the dialog closes.
A dialog opened from a dialog stacks above it; Escape closes the top one first and focus returns to its trigger in the first.
The long title wraps, never cut: it is the question being asked.
No native title attribute.

In Desk the title and the close control sit inside the title bar, so they are parts of TitleBar and WindowControls there (a part belongs to the nearest root). The dialog's own parts in Desk are titlebar, description, body and footer; title, close and controls are listed here for Studio and for style.json optionalParts.

dismissible false is for short waits, while the dialog's own action runs. The app must set it back to true when the action ends, success or failure. The close control (the Studio IconButton or the Desk close light) is aria-disabled and stays focusable.
Development builds warn in the console when a dialog opens with no title, and when its footer holds more than three actions.

A form in a dialog: the form element lives in DialogBody with an id and an onSubmit; the submit Button sits in DialogFooter with type="submit" and form={id}, so Enter in a field and the button both submit. Close the dialog from onSubmit when the save succeeds, not from a DialogClose around the submit button.

en.title: The question being asked, in sentence case: Delete the project Spring launch? A task title is fine for a form: Create a board.
en.description: One sentence that says what happens: Its 12 boards go to the trash for 30 days.
en.buttons: Verb plus noun: Delete project, Keep project. Never OK, Yes, Continue or Confirm. Cancel first, the primary action last.

ar.title: The question in white Saudi dialect, no diacritics: تبي تحذف المشروع؟
ar.buttons: Noun form labels, no diacritics: حذف المشروع، إبقاء المشروع. Never نعم or موافق.

react.note: The portal is a Theme that copies the axes of the Theme the Dialog is in (the Toaster pattern), so tokens, language and direction apply inside it.

angular.note: Directives dsDialog (on an ng-container), dsDialogTrigger, dsDialogContent (an ng-template), dsDialogClose, dsDialogBody, dsDialogFooter, dsDialogTitle, dsDialogDescription. The layer renders through a CDK ComponentPortal straight into body, so the DOM equals React's: no cdk-dialog-container and no overlay pane. The portal theme copies every axis of the opening dsTheme. Focus trap on the CDK InteractivityChecker; exit waits for getAnimations. The panel also carries aria-modal. Dialog.css is used as is.

native.note: Renders as a sheet on phones

styles.studio: A flat panel: the solid surface, the panel radius, the dialog shadow. The title sits in a band on surface-2 with a line under it and the close IconButton (part close) at its inline end; the footer is a band on surface-2 with a line over it. The backdrop is the scrim with a light blur. The panel rises 4px and scales up from 98% on duration.base.
styles.desk: Renders as a window with traffic lights: glass with a 24px blur, radius 1rem, a hairline inside, the deep window shadow. The title bar (optional part titlebar) starts with the lights (optional part controls): only the close light works, minimize and zoom are idle and out of the tab order, and the close light is part close. The title sits in the bar and wraps when long. The window grows from 92% on the window open timing. In right to left layouts the lights stay at the top left and the title is centered.
styles.neutral: Planned.
styles.liquid: Planned: a glass sheet.

mistakes.wrong: A dialog that only says Saved
mistakes.right: A toast

mistakes.wrong: Buttons that say OK and Cancel
mistakes.right: Verb plus noun: Delete project and Keep project

mistakes.wrong: Focus on the destructive button of a danger dialog
mistakes.right: tone danger and the Cancel action in DialogClose: focus opens on it

mistakes.wrong: A DialogTitle wrapped in a div inside the body
mistakes.right: DialogTitle as a direct child of DialogContent, or the title prop, so it renders once at the top and in the Desk title bar

mistakes.wrong: Hiding the close button in Desk with CSS
mistakes.right: The style turns the titlebar and controls parts on in style.json; Dialog then renders the close light instead of the IconButton

mistakes.wrong: A dialog that closes while its action is still saving
mistakes.right: dismissible false and the primary Button loading until the action ends

mistakes.wrong: Waiting for animationend before removing a closed dialog
mistakes.right: Dialog.css sets the animations to none under reduced motion, so Radix removes the dialog at once

mistakes.wrong: A <form> that wraps the whole DialogContent, or a submit Button inside DialogClose
mistakes.right: <form id="rename" onSubmit={save}> inside DialogBody; <Button type="submit" form="rename" tone="accent" emphasis="solid"> in DialogFooter; close on success

name: DropdownMenu
summary: A menu of actions or options that opens from a trigger button. Items, checkbox and radio items, labels, separators and submenus, with arrow keys, typeahead and Escape.
useWhen: More actions than fit next to the object they act on
A set of related commands behind one button, such as the actions of a board
Options that are switched on and off, or one chosen from a short set, next to the commands they change
avoidWhen: Choosing a value for a form field
Actions that need a right click to find
Rich content, a form or a picture in the panel
One or two actions that fit on the page as buttons
Navigation between pages of a site

open.description: DropdownMenu: controlled open state, with onOpenChange.

onOpenChange.description: DropdownMenu: called with true on open and false on close (an item chosen, Escape, a click outside).

modal.description: DropdownMenu: true hides the rest of the page from assistive tech (aria-hidden) and blocks pointer input outside while open. Default false: the menu button pattern needs neither, and axe flags focusable content under aria-hidden when no aria-modal dialog is open.

size.description: DropdownMenu: row height and type size. sm rows are 24px (size.control.xs), md rows follow menu.item.height (24, 28 and 32px in the compact, default and comfortable densities). Submenus take the size of their menu.

side.description: DropdownMenuContent: where the menu opens, in logical words. block-end is under the trigger; inline-end is after it in reading order, so on its left in Arabic. It flips to the other side when there is no room.

align.description: DropdownMenuContent: how the menu lines up with the trigger. start is the trigger's inline start edge, its right edge in Arabic.

sideOffset.description: DropdownMenuContent: the gap to the trigger in px.

collisionPadding.description: DropdownMenuContent and DropdownMenuSubContent: the space kept from the viewport edge in px. The menu is never taller than the room left: it scrolls inside.

loop.description: DropdownMenuContent: ArrowDown on the last item goes to the first.

DropdownMenuItem.tone.description: An item's tone. danger marks a destructive action: the danger text color, and the label names what is destroyed. The menu root has no tone.

start.description: Items and the sub trigger: leading content, a system icon name or a node. Decorative: the text names the item. Rows without it line their text up with rows that have it.

end.description: Items: trailing content, a system icon name or a node. The sub trigger always shows chevron-forward here, mirrored in RTL.

shortcut.description: Items: a key hint shown at the inline end as plain text, left to right in every language (for example Ctrl+D). It does not bind the key; the app does.

disabled.description: Items and DropdownMenuTrigger: aria-disabled and data-disabled. A disabled item stays in the menu, is skipped by the arrow keys and does not select. Drawn with opacity.disabled.

onSelect.description: Items: runs on click, Enter and Space, then the menu closes. Call event.preventDefault() to keep it open.

checked.description: DropdownMenuCheckboxItem, with onCheckedChange. The check icon shows it, a minus for indeterminate.

value.description: DropdownMenuRadioGroup, with onValueChange: the chosen DropdownMenuRadioItem value.

textValue.description: Items: the text typeahead matches. Default: the label when it is plain text.

DropdownMenuTrigger.description: One child element, a system Button or IconButton, rendered as the trigger (always asChild). It gets aria-haspopup menu, aria-expanded and data-state, names the menu, and takes focus back on close.

DropdownMenuSub.description: A submenu: a DropdownMenuSubTrigger, then a DropdownMenuSubContent. open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange as on the root.

a11y.role: menu (the root and each submenu). Not modal by default: the page stays in the accessibility tree, Tab does not leave the open menu, and a click or focus outside closes it. Items are menuitem, menuitemcheckbox (aria-checked true, false or mixed) and menuitemradio inside a group. The trigger has aria-haspopup menu and aria-expanded, and names the menu (aria-labelledby).
a11y.focus: Opened with Enter, Space or ArrowDown on the trigger: focus on the first item. Opened with ArrowUp: focus on the last item. Opened with the pointer: focus on the menu, the first arrow key goes to an item. The highlight follows the pointer and the keys. On close, focus returns to the trigger.

keys.ArrowDown: On the trigger, opens the menu with focus on the first item. In the menu, moves to the next item, skipping disabled ones
keys.ArrowUp: On the trigger, opens the menu with focus on the last item. In the menu, moves to the previous item
keys.Enter: On the trigger, opens the menu. On an item, selects it and closes the menu; on a sub trigger, opens the submenu
keys.ArrowRight: On a sub trigger, opens the submenu with focus on its first item. In a submenu, nothing. In right to left layouts this is ArrowLeft
keys.ArrowLeft: In a submenu, closes it and returns focus to its sub trigger. In right to left layouts this is ArrowRight
keys.Escape: Closes the menu, or only the open submenu, and returns focus to the trigger
keys.Typeahead: Typing letters moves to the next item whose label starts with them

a11y.announce: The menu is read with the trigger's name when it opens. Each item reads its label, its shortcut, its checked state and whether it is disabled or opens a submenu.
notes: Tab does not move focus while the menu is open (Radix keeps it in the menu); Escape or choosing an item returns focus to the trigger.
Disabled items use aria-disabled: they stay in the menu so a screen reader user learns they exist, and the arrow keys skip them.
Checked state is shown by a check icon, a minus for indeterminate, never by color alone (WCAG 1.4.1).
A danger item is drawn in the danger text color; its label also names the action (Delete board), so color is never the only cue.
The menu never grows past the viewport: it takes the room Radix measures on the open side, minus collisionPadding, and scrolls inside. Rows are at least 24px tall (size.target-min).
Shortcut hints are plain text set left to right, so key names read the same inside Arabic.
The submenu chevron is chevron-forward and mirrors in right to left layouts; the submenu opens toward the inline end and Radix follows the direction set by Theme.

Contract keys: ArrowDown and ArrowUp are checked on the trigger (they open the menu and move focus). Home, End, Enter, Space, the submenu arrows and typeahead are covered by the unit tests, since the generic suite cannot press them inside an open menu.
No native title attribute.

en.trigger: Names the menu: a noun (Board actions, Edit) or a verb plus a noun. An icon only trigger names the object too: More frame actions, never only More.
en.items: Verb plus noun, sentence case: Duplicate board, Copy link. Options are nouns or short phrases: Show grid, Name. No ending punctuation, no ellipsis unless the item opens a dialog that asks for more.
en.label: A short noun over the group: Board, Sort by.
en.danger: Name what is destroyed: Delete board, never Delete alone or Remove.
en.count: Up to 12 entries at the top level. Group or split longer menus, or use a submenu.

ar.items: Noun form labels, white Saudi dialect, no diacritics: تكرار اللوحة، نسخ الرابط، حذف اللوحة.
ar.label: A short noun: اللوحة، الترتيب حسب.
ar.shortcut: Key names stay in Latin letters and left to right: Ctrl+D.

react.note: The content and each submenu are portaled into a Theme that copies the axes of the Theme the menu is in (the Toaster pattern), so tokens, language and direction apply inside. A submenu is its own root carrying data-part sub-content.

styles.studio: A flat surface: surface-3, the card radius (16px) with 12px rows inside, the menu shadow, no border. The lit row takes the overlay step; a danger row a danger tint. Rows use the menu weight. Separators on surface-2.
styles.desk: Glass, from the macOS style menu bar menu: the strong glass material with the strong blur, a hairline, the soft window shadow, the panel radius (12px) with 8px rows inside, regular weight. The lit row is the yellow primary fill with dark text, a danger row lights in the danger fill. Under reduced transparency and more contrast the glass turns solid and the blur goes.
styles.neutral: Planned.
styles.liquid: Planned: a glass menu, never on top of other glass.

mistakes.right: Select, which shows the chosen value in the field

mistakes.right: Name the object: More frame actions

mistakes.right: DropdownMenuCheckboxItem or DropdownMenuRadioItem: the check icon carries the state

mistakes.right: A system Button or IconButton inside DropdownMenuTrigger
