name: EmptyState
summary: A place with no content yet that says what is missing, what to do next and how, with the action that does it.
useWhen: A list, grid, table or panel that has no items yet, the first time someone opens it
A search or a filter that returns nothing, with live set so it is announced
A view that needs a first step from the person before it can show anything, such as connecting an account
avoidWhen: Something failed to load or save: that is an error, not an empty place
Content is still loading
A blocking message that needs a decision
A one word note inside a row or a field, such as None: write it as plain text

size.description: sm inside a list or a card, md for a panel, lg for a whole view. Sets the block padding (space xl, 6xl, 11xl), the icon box and the type sizes. The inline padding stays at space l or xl, so a narrow column keeps its width.

icon.description: A system icon name or a node, in a square on surface 2. 16px at sm, 24px at md and lg. Hidden from assistive tech.

title.description: What is empty, as a heading: No boards yet.

headingLevel.description: The heading level of the title.

children.description: The body: what to do next, naming the mechanism (Create a board, or drag a file onto this page).

actions.description: One or two Buttons. The first is the main action, a verb plus a noun, usually tone accent with emphasis solid.

live.description: Adds role status so the empty state is announced when it replaces content, such as a search with no results. Off for a place that is empty on page load.

a11y.role: None by default; status when live. The title is a heading.
a11y.focus: Not focusable. Tab reaches the actions, in order.

keys.Tab: Moves to the first action, then the next

a11y.announce: Read in order: title, body, actions. With live, the whole region (actions included) is announced once when it appears. Some screen readers miss a live region that mounts with its content; for a sure announcement, mount the EmptyState inside a live region that is already on the page.
notes: The icon is decoration and hidden; the title says what is empty.
Keep live off for a place that is empty when the page opens, so nothing is announced twice.
Shares icon, title, body and actions with ErrorState, which adds details and its own states.

en.title: Name what is missing, sentence case, no end period: No boards yet. For a search: No boards match Spring 2027.
en.body: Say what to do next and name the mechanism: Create a board to plan a project, or drag a file onto this page to import it. No blame, no exclamation marks.
en.actions: A verb plus a noun: Create board, Clear search. Never OK or Continue.

ar.title: White Saudi dialect, no diacritics: ما فيه لوحات.
ar.body: Say what to do next plainly, Western digits.
ar.actions: Noun form labels: إنشاء لوحة، استيراد ملف.

react.note: No motion of its own: fade-rise names how a parent brings it in, from the 1.11 catalog list.

angular.note: dsEmptyState on the host with icon, title and headingLevel inputs; body and actions projected. EmptyState.css as is.

native.note: A centered View with the same parts; the title with accessibilityRole header.

styles.studio: Centered, no surface of its own; the icon sits in a surface 2 square with radius.panel.
styles.desk: The same on Desk's surfaces and type. No recipe.
styles.neutral: Planned: no recipe expected.
styles.liquid: Planned: no recipe expected.

mistakes.wrong: A title that only says Nothing here
mistakes.right: Name what is missing and what to do: No boards yet, then Create a board

mistakes.wrong: An empty state shown while the data is still loading
mistakes.right: Skeleton until the request ends, then the empty state

mistakes.wrong: An empty state for a failed request
mistakes.right: ErrorState with a way to try again

mistakes.wrong: Three or more actions of equal weight
mistakes.right: One main action, at most one quiet one

name: ErrorState
summary: Stands in for a section or a page that failed to load: says what happened, what to do next, and offers a retry, with the error code behind a disclosure.
useWhen: A section, a panel or a page could not load its content
A load can be retried, or there is another way forward such as going back
Replacing skeletons after a load failed
avoidWhen: The content loaded but is empty
An action the person took failed and the page still works
A problem with one form field
A page wide notice that stays while the rest of the page works

title.description: What happened, naming the thing: Could not load members.

body.description: What to do next and what is safe.

icon.description: A system icon name, a node, or false for none. Hidden from assistive tech.

size.description: sm inside a card or panel, md for a section, lg for a whole page.

headingLevel.description: The heading level of the title, to fit the page outline.

onRetry.description: Renders the retry Button first in the actions (accent solid, refresh icon, data-part retry) and is called by it.

retryLabel.description: A verb plus a noun. Arabic default under lang ar: إعادة التحميل.

retrying.description: A retry is in flight: data-state retrying, and the retry Button shows loading with a hidden status.

retryingLabel.description: What the retry Button's hidden status says while retrying.

actions.description: More Buttons after retry, a verb plus a noun: Open boards.

code.description: The error code, inside the details disclosure, left to right in every language.

details.description: More detail inside the disclosure, after the code: a request id to send to support.

detailsOpen.description: Renders the details open at first.

live.description: role alert on the root, so an error that replaces content after load is read once. false for an error present at page load: the root is then role group named by its title, with no live role.

a11y.role: alert while live (default), with aria-atomic false; otherwise a group named by its title. The title is a real heading (h2 by default). The details part is a native details element.
a11y.focus: Focus does not move to it. Tab reaches the retry Button, the other actions, then the details summary.

keys.Tab: Moves to the retry Button, the other actions, then the details summary
keys.Enter: Runs the focused action, or opens and closes the details
keys.Space: Runs the focused action, or opens and closes the details

a11y.announce: With live, the role alert (aria-atomic false, so a retry does not read it all again) reads the title, body and actions once when the error replaces content after load. Retrying is said by the retry Button's hidden status (Retrying). An error present at page load is not announced; pass live false there.
notes: The retry Button stays focusable while retrying (aria-disabled through loading), so focus is not lost.
The summary is at least 24px tall (WCAG 2.5.8) and draws the focus ring from the focus tokens.

en.title: Say what failed and name the thing: Could not load members. Not Oops or Something went wrong alone.
en.body: What to do next and what is safe: Check your connection, then retry. Your draft is safe.
en.actions: A verb plus a noun: Retry loading, Open boards. Never OK, Continue, Confirm or Yes.
en.code: The code as the system gives it, for support. Not the only explanation.

ar.title: Noun forms, no diacritics: تعذر تحميل الأعضاء.
ar.actions: Noun form labels: إعادة التحميل، فتح اللوحات.
ar.code: The code stays left to right; Western digits.

native.note: The details disclosure becomes a pressable row that shows the code.

styles.studio: Tokens only: a danger tint tile behind the icon, muted body text.
styles.desk: Tokens only; the retry Button is the yellow primary.
styles.neutral: Tokens only.

mistakes.wrong: Something went wrong, with nothing else
mistakes.right: Could not load members. Check your connection, then retry.

mistakes.wrong: The error code as the only message
mistakes.right: Plain words first; the code behind Error details

mistakes.wrong: A retry that blanks the section while it runs
mistakes.right: Keep the ErrorState with retrying set, then swap in skeletons or content

mistakes.wrong: ErrorState for a list that loaded with no items
mistakes.right: EmptyState

name: Field
summary: Wires one label, one description and one error message to one form control, and passes the invalid, disabled, read only and required state to it.
useWhen: Any form control that needs a visible label
A control with a hint that helps fill it, or an error that says how to fix the value
A settings row with the label at the start and the control at the end (orientation horizontal)
avoidWhen: A search box in a toolbar whose purpose is plain from an icon and an aria-label
A group of checkboxes or radios that shares one question
Read only text that is not a control

orientation.description: vertical: label above the control. horizontal: label at the start of the control's line.

invalid.description: Marks the control invalid. When not passed, the field is invalid while an error message shows. false hides the error.

readOnly.description: Passed to the control. Still focusable and readable.

required.description: Shows the required mark and sets aria-required on the control.

a11y.role: none on the root. The label is a native label bound to the control with for and id.
a11y.focus: The root is never focusable. Clicking the label focuses the control.

keys.Tab: Moves to the control. The field adds no stop of its own.

a11y.announce: The description, then the error, are read with the control through aria-describedby when focus lands there. The error is not a live region and never role alert, so an error that is there when the page loads does not interrupt.
notes: The required mark is an asterisk glyph, so it does not rely on color, and it is aria-hidden. The control carries aria-required, not the native required attribute, so the browser shows no validation bubble.
The error starts with a danger icon, so it does not rely on color.
Controls read the wiring with useFieldControl(): id, aria-describedby, aria-invalid, aria-required, disabled and readOnly. A value the control passes itself wins.
A form that checks on submit moves focus to the first invalid control.
Validate on blur or on submit, never on every key. On submit, move focus to the first invalid control.

en.label: A noun in sentence case that names the value: Email, Board name. No colon, no question.
en.description: One sentence that helps fill the field or says where the value shows. Not a repeat of the label.
en.error: Says what to do, in plain words: Add the part after the @. Never only Invalid or Required.
en.placeholder: Never the label. An example value at most: For example, spring launch.
en.required: Mark required fields with * and say once, above the form, that fields marked * are required.

ar.label: اسم بصيغة المصدر أو الاسم، بدون تشكيل: البريد الإلكتروني، اسم اللوحة
ar.description: جملة وحدة توضح وش يكتب أو وين تظهر القيمة
ar.error: يقول وش يسوي عشان يصلحها: البريد ناقص، اكتبه كامل. مو بس غلط
ar.placeholder: ما يكون بديل عن العنوان. مثال على القيمة بس
ar.latin: النص اللاتيني داخل العربي يمر عبر Bidi
ar.required: سطر واحد فوق النموذج: الحقول اللي عليها * مطلوبة

styles.studio: Semibold label, muted description, danger text error with an icon
styles.desk: The same, in Instrument Sans

mistakes.wrong: A placeholder used as the label
mistakes.right: A FieldLabel above the control, and an example value in the placeholder at most

mistakes.wrong: An error that only says Invalid email
mistakes.right: An error that says how to fix it: Add the part after the @, for example name@example.com

mistakes.wrong: role alert on an inline error that is there when the page loads
mistakes.right: FieldError, read through aria-describedby when focus lands on the control

mistakes.wrong: A red asterisk as the only sign of a required field
mistakes.right: required on Field: an aria-hidden asterisk glyph plus aria-required on the control

mistakes.wrong: A label with an id written by hand and a control with a different id
mistakes.right: Field gives both ids. A control id of its own is picked up by the label.

name: Grid
summary: Lays out children in columns and rows: a fixed column count, or as many columns as fit at a minimum item size.
useWhen: Cards, files or tiles of the same kind that line up in columns and rows
A form or settings page with two or three columns on wide screens and one on phones
A twelve column page layout where some cells span more columns
avoidWhen: Items in one line or one column only
Tiles of deliberately mixed sizes on an overview or landing section
Tabular data a person compares across rows
A visual order that differs from the reading order

columns.description: A number from 1 to 12 gives equal tracks. auto-fit fits as many columns as minItemSize allows and grows them to fill the row. Fixed counts fall to one column under breakpoint.phone unless keepColumns is set. Sets data-columns.

minItemSize.description: The smallest item width with auto-fit: sm 10rem, md 15rem, lg 24rem, derived from the breakpoint tokens until a size.grid scale exists. Capped at 100% of the grid, so one item never overflows at 320px. Sets data-min.

gap.description: Space between cells on both axes, a space.* step.

rowGap.description: Space between rows when it differs from gap.

keepColumns.description: Keeps a fixed column count on phones. Sets data-keep-columns. Only for short cells, such as a calendar or a keypad.

as.description: The element to render. ul and ol get role list and lose their bullets; use GridItem as li inside.

GridItem.span.description: Columns the item spans; full spans the whole row. Sets data-span. On phones every item fills the one column.

GridItem.rowSpan.description: Rows the item spans. Sets data-row-span.

GridItem.as.description: The element of the item. li inside a list Grid.

children.description: The cells, plain elements or GridItem.

a11y.role: none of its own: a div, or list on ul and ol
a11y.focus: Never focusable. Focus and reading order are the DOM order: cells fill from the start side, the right in Arabic.
a11y.announce: Nothing. A Grid is layout only.
notes: This is a layout grid, not role grid. A grid of interactive cells with arrow key navigation is a different component (DataGrid).
No dense packing and no order property: the visual order must match the DOM order (WCAG 1.3.2, 2.4.3).
One column under breakpoint.phone and capped track minimums keep the page free of sideways scroll at 320px (WCAG 1.4.10).

en.items: No copy of its own. Cells carry their own labels.

ar.items: No copy of its own. Cells fill from the right in Arabic because the tracks follow dir.

react.note: No motion: a static layout has nothing to animate, so no pattern from the catalog applies. The phone fallback is a viewport media query; a Grid in a narrow sidebar on a wide screen keeps its columns, so use auto-fit there.

angular.note: The host element is the root and the item, so as is not needed.

native.note: No CSS grid in React Native: fixed columns map to a percentage basis per item and auto-fit to a basis from onLayout width.

styles.studio: Layout only. The gap follows density.
styles.desk: Layout only. The gap follows density.
styles.neutral: Layout only. The gap follows density.
styles.liquid: Layout only. The gap follows density.

mistakes.wrong: columns 4 with fixed pixel widths on each cell
mistakes.right: columns 4, or auto-fit with minItemSize, so tracks shrink and fall to one column on phones

mistakes.wrong: A GridItem span larger than an auto-fit grid has tracks
mistakes.right: span full, or a fixed column count, since auto-fit has fewer tracks on narrow screens

mistakes.wrong: keepColumns on a grid of cards with text
mistakes.right: Leave the phone fallback on; keepColumns is for short cells like a keypad

mistakes.wrong: role grid on a layout Grid
mistakes.right: No role; arrow key navigation between cells belongs to DataGrid

mistakes.wrong: keepColumns with a GridItem span larger than the column count
mistakes.right: Spans no larger than columns; on phones keepColumns keeps the count, so a wider span adds a track and scrolls sideways

name: Icon
summary: One system icon drawn from the icon set of the active style, sized by the size.icon tokens.
useWhen: A glyph next to a label in a control, a menu item or a status line
An icon only control, where the control carries the accessible name
A status glyph that a label beside it already explains
avoidWhen: An icon that is the only way to tell a meaning and has no label
A brand logo or an illustration
A glyph drawn from a file outside the system names

name.description: A system icon name. Directional names say forward and back.

size.description: 12, 16 and 24 px. The numbers are accepted too.

set.description: An icon set id, pixel or line. Overrides the set of the active style.

label.description: Gives the icon role img and this accessible name. Without it the icon is hidden.

a11y.role: img when label is set, otherwise hidden with aria-hidden
a11y.focus: Never focusable.
notes: Icons are decoration by default. The control around them carries the name.
Names in the mirror list flip in right to left layouts. Brand marks, clocks and media controls never flip.

The host svg is the root, glyph nodes come from the Renderer (no innerHTML), the style's icon set comes from dsTheme through the DS_ICON_STYLE signal. Used by dsButton and dsIconButton. No Angular demo yet, so the contract suite does not cover it on its own.

styles.desk: Pixel set, crisp edges

name: IconButton
summary: A square action button with only an icon. Its label is the accessible name and the text of its Tooltip.
useWhen: A toolbar, a header or a row where the icon is well known: close, more, settings
A repeated action in a list where a text label would crowd the row
A close control in a dialog, a panel or a toast
avoidWhen: The icon alone does not say what happens
The main action of a form or a dialog
A choice that stays on or off

insteadUse.The main action of a view: Button with tone accent and emphasis solid

icon.description: A system icon name or a node. Hidden from assistive tech. 16px at every size, lg included, as in both sources.

label.description: The accessible name, set as aria-label. A verb plus a noun. Never the native title attribute. The Tooltip pairing that shows it on hover arrives with Tooltip in wave 1.

size.description: A square of size.control: 24, 28, 32 and 44 px. Never under 24 by 24.

emphasis.description: ghost, because icon buttons sit in toolbars and headers. No link: an icon only link reads as neither.

shape.description: pill is a circle, square takes radius.sm, default takes radius.control (a circle in Desk).

loading.description: The spinner replaces the icon, a visually hidden status says loadingLabel, aria-busy is set, activation is blocked, focus stays.

loadingLabel.description: What the hidden status says while loading.

disabled.description: aria-disabled and data-disabled. Stays focusable so a Tooltip can say why.

asChild.description: Renders the single child element, for example an empty link, as the button.

a11y.role: button (native button element), or the role of the asChild element
a11y.focus: In the tab order in every state. A 2px ring on keyboard focus; solid fills get the doubled ring.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the next control

a11y.announce: The label prop is the accessible name. While loading, a visually hidden status says loadingLabel and aria-busy is set.
notes: label is required by the type, so an icon button always has a name.
At least 24 by 24 CSS px at xs (WCAG 2.5.8). Use lg (44px) in touch layouts.
No native title attribute. The Tooltip pairing that shows the label on hover and focus arrives with Tooltip in wave 1.
Directional icons (chevron-back, arrow-forward) mirror in right to left layouts.
A disabled asChild link loses its href and keeps role link.

en.label: A verb plus a noun in sentence case: Close panel, Open settings. Not the icon name.

ar.label: Noun form, no diacritics: إغلاق اللوحة، فتح الإعدادات.

styles.neutral: Planned.

mistakes.right: label set; the hint in a Tooltip

mistakes.right: label="Delete file"

name: Input
summary: A single line text input: a native input in a bordered box with optional start and end adornments.
useWhen: A short value typed on one line: a name, an email, a link, a number
A search box, with the search icon at the start
A value with a unit or a currency shown inside the box
avoidWhen: Text longer than one line
A choice from a known list
A date, a color or a file

size.description: Height from size.control: 24, 28, 32 and 44 px at default density.

shape.description: default takes radius.control from the style, a pill in Studio and Desk. pill is always fully round.

invalid.description: Marks the value invalid. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

disabled.description: Inside a Field it follows the Field.

readOnly.description: Still focusable, selectable and readable. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

required.description: Sets aria-required. Inside a Field it follows the Field.

start.description: An icon name, a short text such as $, or a node. Icon names and texts are aria-hidden.

end.description: An icon name, a short text such as px, or a node. Icon names and texts are aria-hidden.

rootProps.description: Props for the root box. className and style also go to the root; every other native prop and the ref go to the input.

a11y.role: textbox, from the native input (spinbutton for type number, searchbox for type search)
a11y.focus: The input is the only tab stop. Clicking anywhere in the box that is not interactive focuses the input. Focus shows the glow and a 2px ring around the box.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the input, and on to the next control
keys.Home, End: Move the caret to the start or the end of the value
keys.ArrowUp, ArrowDown: Change the value for type number
keys.Escape: Clears the value for type search, as the browser does

a11y.announce: Name from the Field label. The Field description and error through aria-describedby. aria-invalid and aria-required from the Field.

name: Kbd
summary: A key or a keyboard shortcut drawn as keycaps, with the key names spoken to screen readers.
useWhen: Telling people which key or shortcut runs an action: Ctrl+K opens search
The shortcut part of a menu item, a tooltip or a command palette row
A keyboard help sheet that lists shortcuts next to what they do
avoidWhen: Code, a file name or a command people type, which is not a key press
A label on a button people click
The only way to learn an action: a shortcut is an extra path, the action needs a visible control too

insteadUse.Code or a command people type: Code (wave 2), or a monospace text span
insteadUse.A hint that explains a control: Tooltip, with Kbd in its shortcut part

children.description: The key or the shortcut. A string is split into keycaps by splitShortcut: Mod+K, Ctrl+Shift+P, ⌘⇧P, Esc, Ctrl++ or ⌘+ for the plus key. Plus is the only separator. Mod is Command on a Mac and Control elsewhere; on a Mac the modifiers are drawn in Apple order (⌃⌥⇧⌘). A node draws one keycap as is; give it a label, or the node itself stays readable.

size.description: Keycap height: xs 16 (size.icon.md), sm 20, md 24 (size.icon.lg) px. Use xs or sm inside menus, tooltips and running text.

platform.description: The convention to draw. mac: symbols and no separators (⌘⇧P). other: names joined by plus (Ctrl+Shift+P). Default: mac under a Theme with platform ios, otherwise the user agent after hydration; the server draws other.

label.description: What screen readers say instead of the spoken key names (Control Shift P by default), for example names in another language.

decorative.description: Hides the whole root from assistive tech and drops the spoken copy. For a shortcut next to an action that already carries aria-keyshortcuts.

separator.description: Drawn between keycaps. Default plus on other and nothing on mac.

a11y.role: None: a kbd element. Each keycap is hidden; a visually hidden span (spoken) says the key names, so a screen reader hears Control Shift P, not C T R L plus.
a11y.focus: Never focusable.
a11y.announce: The spoken key names, or label. Nothing when decorative.
notes: The root is dir ltr and isolated (unicode-bidi isolate), so a shortcut reads Ctrl then K inside an Arabic sentence and does not move the punctuation around it.
Menu items and buttons that have a shortcut set aria-keyshortcuts (ariaKeyShortcuts from the same helpers) and render Kbd decorative.
No hover, press or motion: a keycap is text, not a control.
Under forced colors the gradient and the depth shadow drop; each key keeps a CanvasText border.
The default spoken names are English and carry lang en, so an Arabic page reads them with an English voice. Pass label for names in another language.

en.keys: Key names as printed on keyboards: Ctrl, Shift, Alt, Esc, Enter, Tab, single letters in upper case.
en.sentence: Put the shortcut after the verb: Press Ctrl+K to open search.

ar.keys: Keys stay in Latin letters and read left to right: Ctrl+K, never translated or mirrored.
ar.sentence: اضغط Ctrl+K للبحث. The key names are spoken in English by default; pass label for another wording.

react.note: Parsing, the Mod mapping and spoken names live in @the-system/shared (shortcut.ts), so Angular and native read the same keys.

native.note: Touch first apps rarely show shortcuts; useful on iPad and Android with a hardware keyboard. Same shortcut.ts.

styles.studio: A dark sculpted keycap: gradient face, top highlight, bottom edge and a soft drop, from the kbd tokens.
styles.desk: The same keycap on the Desk tokens.
styles.neutral: Light keycap from the kbd tokens of the Neutral style once it lands; no recipe.

name: Link
summary: Navigation to another page, place or site, inside a sentence or on its own line. Always underlined.
useWhen: Navigation inside running text: a sentence that points to a guide, a policy or a setting
A link that stands on its own line under a card, a form or an empty state, with standalone
A link to another site, with external, so it opens a new tab and says so
A router link that must look like text, through asChild
avoidWhen: An action that changes data or starts a task on this page (save, send, delete)
The main call to action of a view that must read as a button
Navigation between sections of the app shell or between tabs of one view
Link text that only says Click here, Here or More

href.description: Where the link goes. Removed while disabled.

tone.description: neutral reads as color.text.link, accent as color.primary.on-surface (the yellow family in Desk).

size.description: Font size from font.size xs, s, m and l. No default: without size the link inherits the font size of the text around it, which is what a link in a sentence wants.

external.description: Opens a new tab (target _blank, rel noopener noreferrer unless passed) and renders the end part: the external icon, mirrored in RTL, and visually hidden words after a comma.

externalLabel.description: The hidden words of an external link. Under an Arabic Theme the default is يفتح في تبويب جديد.

standalone.description: A link on its own line: an inline flex box at least size.target-min (24px) tall. Sets data-standalone. Leave it off inside a sentence, where the inline target exception of WCAG 2.5.8 applies.

disabled.description: Removes the href, sets role link, aria-disabled and data-disabled, and keeps the link in the tab order so a Tooltip can say why. Click and middle click do nothing.

asChild.description: Renders the single child element, for example a router link, as the link. A disabled child loses its href.

children.description: The link text. It names the place, not the gesture.

a11y.role: link (native a with href; role link is set while disabled, when the href is gone)
a11y.focus: In the tab order, disabled included. A 2px ring from focus.shadow.ring on keyboard focus, drawn around every line of a link that wraps.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the next control

a11y.announce: The label is the accessible name. An external link adds the hidden words after a comma: Open the docs, opens in a new tab.
notes: The underline is drawn at rest and on hover, so a link in running text is never told apart by color alone (WCAG 1.4.1). Hover makes it thicker.
Inline target exception (WCAG 2.5.8): a link inside a sentence keeps the line height of the text and may be under 24px tall. A link on its own line takes standalone and is at least 24px tall.
Space does not follow a link, only Enter, as in the browser.
The external icon is hidden from assistive tech; the hidden words carry the meaning.
Under forced colors the system link color applies, the underline takes the text color and the focus outline uses Highlight.
No native title attribute. Hints come from Tooltip.

en.label: Name the destination in sentence case: Read the pricing guide, the sharing guide. Never Click here, Here, More or Learn more on its own.
en.sentence: Put the link on the words that say where it goes, not on a whole sentence.
en.external: Do not write opens in a new tab in the visible text: external adds it for screen readers and the icon shows it.

ar.label: Noun form, no diacritics: دليل المشاركة، سياسة الخصوصية. Never اضغط هنا.
ar.sentence: Link only the words that name the place, and keep Latin runs in Bidi.

react.note: No motion: color and underline swap at once on hover, so there is no pattern to name and nothing to reduce.

angular.note: The host anchor is the root. No asChild: a[dsLink] on a routerLink anchor is the router form.

native.note: A pressable Text inside running text; Linking.openURL for external links.

styles.studio: Bright text (color.text.link) with a soft control colored underline that turns to the text color and thickens on hover. Accent reads the same as neutral in Studio, since its primary is the neutral fill.
styles.desk: Accent is the yellow family: color.primary.on-surface, yellow on dark and a dark gold on light, with a yellow underline. Neutral matches Studio.
styles.neutral: Takes the tokens of the Neutral style, no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: Link text Click here or Learn more
mistakes.right: Link text that names the place: Read the pricing guide

mistakes.wrong: A link told apart from the sentence by color only
mistakes.right: Link, which keeps the underline at rest

mistakes.right: A Button; a link only navigates

name: List
summary: A vertical list of rows, each with a title and optional start, description, end and actions. Rows can be links.
useWhen: A short list of things people open: mail, files, boards, members
Rows that each carry one or two actions, such as delete or more
Ordered steps or a ranking, as an ol
avoidWhen: Picking one or more options from the rows
Many fields per row that people compare across rows
Term and value pairs about one thing
Site or app navigation with sections and nesting

size.description: md rows are at least list.row.height plus a small inset (about 36px in the default density), sm rows are list.row.height (28px default, 24 compact, 32 comfortable).

variant.description: plain: rows only. divided: a hairline between rows. inset: rows grouped on a rounded surface with hairlines. Sets data-variant on the root.

ordered.description: Renders an ol for rows whose order means something.

empty.description: Shown when there are no rows, in a p with part empty; the root is then a div. Say what is missing and what to do next.

ListItem.title.description: The row's main text, one line with an ellipsis. With href it is the link.

ListItem.description.description: A second line, up to two lines then an ellipsis.

ListItem.start.description: A system icon name (hidden from assistive tech) or a node such as an Avatar.

ListItem.end.description: Trailing content that is not an action: a time, a count, a Badge.

ListItem.actions.description: Buttons or IconButtons for the row. Their own Tab stops, drawn above the row link.

ListItem.href.description: Makes the row a link: the title becomes an anchor whose hit area covers the row.

ListItem.linkProps.description: Extra anchor props: target, rel, onClick for a client router, aria-current.

ListItem.active.description: The current row. Sets data-active, the active fill, and aria-current (true, or the value in linkProps) on the link. The description and end step up to the default text color on the active fill.

ListItem.disabled.description: Dims the start icon and the title. A link loses its href, keeps role link with aria-disabled and leaves the tab order. The description and end stay at full contrast, so the reason the row is off stays readable. Actions are the caller's to disable.

a11y.role: list (ul or ol) with listitem rows. A linked row's title is a link. An empty list is a div with a paragraph, so it is not read as a list of one.
a11y.focus: Each linked row is one Tab stop on its title link; its actions follow. Rows without a link and the list itself are not focusable. A 2px ring from focus.shadow.ring draws around the whole row.

keys.Tab: Moves to the next row link or row action
keys.Shift+Tab: Moves to the previous row link or row action
keys.Enter: Follows the focused row link, or activates the focused action

a11y.announce: The link name is the title only; the description, end and actions are read as the row's other content. Name each action with the row it acts on: Delete mail from Sara.
notes: No arrow key navigation: this is a list of links and buttons, not a composite widget. For arrow keys and selection use ListBox.
The row link's hit area is its ::before stretched over the row, which is also the focus layer. Actions are positioned later in the DOM, so they sit above it without a z-index.
Give the list an aria-label when the page has no heading for it.
Under forced colors the focus ring is Highlight, the active row gets a CanvasText outline and separators are CanvasText.

en.title: A name people scan for: the sender, the file, the board. Sentence case.
en.description: One line of context: the subject, the last change.
en.empty: What is missing and what happens next: No mail yet. Mail you get from your team shows here.
en.actions: Accessible names say the verb and the row: Delete mail from Sara Alqahtani.

ar.title: Noun form, no diacritics.
ar.empty: ما فيه رسائل للحين. الرسائل اللي توصلك من فريقك بتظهر هنا.
ar.digits: Western digits in end content such as times and counts.

native.note: FlatList rows with Pressable for linked rows; 44pt rows on iOS and 48dp on Android.

styles.studio: Flat rows, a 5 percent overlay on hover, a 10 percent overlay for the active row; inset groups on surface 2.
styles.desk: The same on the Desk tokens; inset groups read as a panel inside a window.
styles.neutral: The same on the Neutral tokens; no recipe.

name: Meter
summary: A measured value in a known range, such as storage used or a score, with its level in words.
useWhen: A value that sits in a fixed range and is not a task: storage used, a quota, a score, a signal strength
A value whose regions matter (plenty of room, filling up, almost full), set with low, high and optimum
A list of measures to compare, one small meter per row
avoidWhen: A task that moves toward done
A value with no known maximum
A rating the person sets

value.description: The measured value. Clamped into [min, max].

max.description: The top of the range. A max at or below min falls back to min plus 100.

low.description: The top of the low region, as in the HTML meter element. Default: no low region.

high.description: The bottom of the high region. Default: no high region.

optimum.description: The best value. Its region gives tone success, the next region warning, the far region danger. Without it, or without low and high, the tone is accent.

label.description: Visible text that names the measure and labels the meter through aria-labelledby. Without it, pass aria-label.

valueText.description: (value, min, max) => string for the visible value and aria-valuetext: 72 GB of 100 GB. Default: a whole percent of the range, rounded down, Western digits.

levelLabels.description: An object of words per level, { low, medium, high }, said after the value: Almost full. Default Low, Medium, High; Arabic منخفض، متوسط، مرتفع under lang ar.

showLevel.description: Shows the level word after the value. Default true when low or high is set. aria-valuetext keeps the level word whenever low or high is set.

tone.description: Overrides the tone the thresholds give. Prefer thresholds, so tone and level agree.

size.description: Track thickness 4, 8 and 12 px; the text steps from font.size.xs to m.

a11y.role: meter, with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuetext
a11y.focus: Never focusable.
a11y.announce: Not a live region. A screen reader reads the label and aria-valuetext, which holds the value and the level word: 72 GB of 100 GB, Filling up.
notes: data-level on the root is low, medium or high. It is a valued attribute, so it is not listed in states: the contract suite reads every data-* entry there as a boolean (see the lane 5B report).
The level is in data-level, in the visible value text and in aria-valuetext, never only in the color.
Thresholds follow the HTML meter: low and high are clamped into the range, and high is never below low.
The indicator scales from the inline start: it fills from the right in Arabic.
Under forced colors the track has a CanvasText border and the indicator is Highlight.
With no optimum the tone is accent: no region is better than another. The HTML meter would assume the midpoint; this is a deliberate choice for Angular to copy.

en.label: Name the measure as a noun: Storage used, Accessibility score.
en.value: Say the amount in its own unit when it means more than a percent: 72 GB of 100 GB.
en.level: Say what the level means for the person: Plenty of room, Filling up, Almost full.
en.language: Pass valueText and levelLabels in the same language: the default level words follow the theme lang, the caller's value text does not.

ar.label: Noun form labels, no diacritics: المساحة المستخدمة.
ar.level: Short noun phrases: المساحة كافية، المساحة تقل، المساحة قربت تخلص.

react.note: Level and tone logic in level.ts (pure, to move to packages/shared). Values formatted by the ProgressBar format.ts helper until packages/shared/src/number.ts lands. Motion: a value change eases the scaleX transform over duration.slow; number-roll names that change until the 1.11 catalog has a fill pattern.

styles.studio: The ProgressBar track; with no thresholds the fill is the strongest text color.
styles.desk: The same track; with no thresholds the fill is yellow on dark and dark gold on light.
styles.neutral: Planned: the brand color with no thresholds.
styles.liquid: Planned: a solid track on content.

mistakes.wrong: A Meter for an upload
mistakes.right: A ProgressBar: an upload is a task

mistakes.wrong: Only the red color when storage is almost full
mistakes.right: high and optimum thresholds and a level word such as Almost full

mistakes.wrong: tone set by hand that disagrees with the level
mistakes.right: low, high and optimum, and let the meter pick the tone

mistakes.wrong: showLevel false, or a hand set tone, with no level in visible text
mistakes.right: Keep the level word visible, or say the level in text next to the meter

name: NotificationCenter
summary: The panel of notifications: a list grouped by day or by the consumer's groups, unread marks, mark all read, actions per item and an empty state. Placed by the consumer in a Popover or a Sheet.
useWhen: A place where a person reviews what happened while they were away: mentions, invites, finished exports
Notifications that stay until read, with an unread count on a bell button
Notifications that carry their own actions, such as accepting an invite
avoidWhen: Telling the person about something that just happened while they watch
A full activity history with search and filters
A single message about the page

items.description: NotificationItem[]: { id, title, body?, time (Date, timestamp or ISO), unread?, tone?, icon?, actions? (up to two { label, onAction }), group? }. Rendered in the given order; the consumer sorts, newest first.

title.description: The panel heading. Arabic default under lang ar.

headingLevel.description: The title's heading level; group labels take the next level.

onMarkAllRead.description: Renders the mark all read Button (data-part mark-all) while any item is unread, and is called by it. The consumer clears unread on its items.

markAllLabel.description: A verb plus a noun. Arabic: تحديد الكل كمقروء.

size.description: sm for a narrow popover: tighter padding and font.size.s.

now.description: The clock for relative times and day groups. Default the time of render. The consumer re-renders to refresh the times.

a11y.role: A section named by its title. Each group is a group named by its heading (a heading level below the title) holding a list; each item is an article in a list item, named by its title, with a time element. Not role feed.
a11y.focus: Every item is a tab stop with a focus ring, so a keyboard user can reach and read each one; its actions follow it. No roving focus, no arrow keys.

keys.Tab: Moves to mark all read, then each item and its actions in order

a11y.announce: The panel never announces. A new notification is announced once by the consumer through toast(); the panel only lists it. The count is plain text.
notes: Unread is never color alone: a dot, a bold title and a visually hidden word (Unread) before the title.
Times use Intl.RelativeTimeFormat with numeric auto; Arabic uses Western digits (nu-latn). The time element carries the ISO time.
Group headings come from the day of each time (Today, Yesterday, Earlier) unless items name a group.

en.item: Who did what to which thing: Sara mentioned you in Launch plan. Sentence case.
en.actions: A verb plus a noun: Accept invite, Open comment. Two at most.
en.empty: Say what shows up here: Mentions, invites and comments on your boards show up here.

ar.item: No diacritics; names as written: سارة أشارت لك في خطة الإطلاق.
ar.actions: Noun form labels: قبول الدعوة، فتح التعليق.
ar.digits: Western digits in times and counts.

native.note: A SectionList with a header per group; items as pressable rows.

styles.studio: Tokens only: no surface of its own, hairline separators, unread rows on overlay-5.
styles.desk: Tokens only; the unread dot takes the yellow primary border.
styles.neutral: Tokens only.

mistakes.wrong: The panel announcing each new item through a live region
mistakes.right: Announce once through toast(); the panel only lists

mistakes.wrong: Unread shown only by a tinted row
mistakes.right: The dot, the bold title and the hidden word come with unread

mistakes.wrong: Wrapping the panel in its own overlay
mistakes.right: Put it in a Popover from a bell IconButton, or a Sheet on phones

mistakes.wrong: Times written as 2026-11-12T14:55
mistakes.right: Pass the time; it renders 5 minutes ago with the ISO time in datetime

name: ProgressBar
summary: A labelled bar that shows how far a task has come, or that it runs with no known end.
useWhen: A task that reports how far it is: an upload, an export, an import
A task with no known end that takes more than a few seconds and has a name, as the indeterminate form
A list of tasks, one small bar per row
avoidWhen: A measured value that is not a task, such as storage used or a score
A short wait on a small area with no value
Little room, such as a card corner or a file chip
Steps the person moves through, such as a form wizard

value.description: Progress from 0 to max. null or undefined gives the indeterminate form. Values out of range are clamped.

max.description: The value that means done. The minimum is always 0 (Radix Progress).

label.description: Visible text that names the task and labels the progressbar through aria-labelledby. Without it, pass aria-label.

showValue.description: Shows the value text at the end of the label row: the percent, or the loading words while indeterminate.

valueText.description: (value, max) => string. Builds both the visible value and aria-valuetext, for example 3 of 10 files. Default: a whole percent in the page language with Western digits.

loadingLabel.description: What the value and aria-valuetext say while indeterminate. Arabic default under lang ar: جار التحميل.

size.description: Track thickness 4, 8 and 12 px (space.fixed.2xs, m, xl); the text steps from font.size.xs to m.

tone.description: Indicator color. accent is color.primary.on-surface; the others are color.state.<tone>.solid.

a11y.role: progressbar (Radix Progress) with aria-valuemin 0, aria-valuemax, aria-valuenow and aria-valuetext
a11y.focus: Never focusable.
a11y.announce: Not a live region: a screen reader reads the label and the value text when it reaches the bar. aria-valuetext carries the formatted value, or the loading words while indeterminate. To announce a finish, say it once in a Toast or a status line.
notes: The label and the value sit inside the progressbar; its children are presentational, so the label names it through aria-labelledby and the value through aria-valuetext.
Indeterminate slides a 40% segment along the track. Under reduced motion it stops as a full, faded track and the value text says Loading.
The indicator scales from the inline start: it fills from the right in Arabic.
Under forced colors the track has a CanvasText border and the indicator is Highlight.
Tone is never the only signal: the label says what happened (Upload stopped) and the value says how far.
WCAG 2.2.2: the indeterminate loop has no pause control; a busy indicator is essential motion, and it stops under reduced motion.
The percent is rounded down, so an unfinished task never shows 100%.
With showValue false, the stopped indeterminate bar under reduced motion has no visible Loading text; keep showValue on, or say the state in text next to the bar.

en.label: Name the task as a present participle plus a noun: Uploading files, Exporting board. On a stop, say what happened and what to do next.
en.value: A whole percent by default. Count units when they mean more: 3 of 10 files.
en.loading: Loading by default; a more exact verb when known: Preparing export.

ar.label: Noun form labels, no diacritics: رفع الملفات، تصدير اللوحة.

react.note: Value changes ease the scaleX transform over duration.slow. The indeterminate loop is named after the spinner pattern of the 1.11 catalog (the looping busy form) until the catalog has a bar form. Values are formatted with Intl.NumberFormat and Western digits in a private helper (format.ts) until packages/shared/src/number.ts lands.

styles.studio: A pill track in overlay 10; the accent indicator is the strongest text color (near white on dark, near black on light), as Studio has a neutral primary.
styles.desk: The same track; the accent indicator is yellow on dark and dark gold on light.
styles.neutral: Planned: the brand color for accent.
styles.liquid: Planned: a solid track; the bar is content, never glass.

mistakes.wrong: A ProgressBar for storage used
mistakes.right: A Meter: storage is a measure, not a task

mistakes.wrong: Only the danger color when an upload fails
mistakes.right: tone danger and a label that says Upload stopped and what to do next

mistakes.wrong: A bar that jumps back to 0 between steps of one task
mistakes.right: One bar for the whole task, or count units with valueText

mistakes.wrong: A bar with no label and no aria-label
mistakes.right: A visible label that names the task, or aria-label when the context names it

name: ProgressCircle
summary: Compact progress in a ring, for a file chip, a card corner or a table cell.
useWhen: Progress of a task in little room: a file chip, a card corner, a table cell, a toolbar
Many small tasks side by side, one ring each, with the name in text next to it
A busy sign that becomes a known value once the task reports one
avoidWhen: There is room for a labelled bar
A measured value that is not a task, such as storage used

name: Stack
summary: Lays out children in one direction, a column or a row, with a gap from the space token scale.
useWhen: Children that sit one under the other with an even gap: form fields, cards in a column, a settings list
A row of controls or chips along the line, wrapping when it runs out of room
Pushing two groups to opposite ends of a row with justify between
avoidWhen: Items that must line up in columns and rows at the same time
Centering a page or capping its width
A gap that must be a pixel number outside the space scale
Space added only to separate two groups with a visible line

direction.description: block runs top to bottom (a column). inline runs along the line from the start side (a row), so it starts on the right in Arabic. Sets data-orientation vertical or horizontal.

gap.description: A space.* step. Fluid, and follows the density axis. Never a number.

align.description: Cross axis alignment (align-items). Logical words only: start is the right edge in a right to left row.

wrap.description: Lets children wrap onto more lines. Sets data-wrap.

as.description: The element to render. ul and ol lose their bullets and get role list, so Safari keeps the list semantics.

asChild.description: Renders the single child element as the Stack through Radix Slot. Wins over as. A ul or ol child loses its bullets, so give it role list yourself.

a11y.role: none of its own: a div by default, the semantics of as or the asChild element otherwise; list on ul and ol
a11y.focus: Never focusable. Focus order is DOM order, which is also the visual order: no reverse directions.
a11y.announce: Nothing. A Stack is layout only.
notes: There is no row-reverse or column-reverse. Reversing the visual order would break the reading and focus order (WCAG 1.3.2, 2.4.3).
Inline direction follows dir: the first child sits on the right in Arabic with no extra prop.

en.items: No copy of its own. Children carry their own labels.

name: Stat

One headline number at the top of a report or a detail page, with how it moved
A count that people compare with a target or the last period
avoidWhen: Many numbers people compare row by row
A trend over time that people read point by point
A number that is a setting people change
A small count on a nav item or a tab

label.description: What the number counts, in sentence case: Active users.

value.description: A number is formatted with Intl in the Theme language with Western digits and the format options. A node (No data) is drawn as is.

format.description: Intl.NumberFormat options for a numeric value: currency, unit, compact notation.

delta.description: The change since the last period. A number sets the trend from its sign and is drawn as its absolute value with deltaFormat (0.12 is 12%). A change that rounds to zero in that format is flat. A delta that is not a finite number is not drawn. A node is drawn as is and needs trend.

deltaFormat.description: Intl.NumberFormat options for a numeric delta.

trend.description: Default from the sign of a numeric delta. Sets data-trend on the root (up, down or flat) and the arrow icon.

tone.description: The color of the change. Default success when up, danger when down, neutral when flat. Set it when down is good: costs, errors, churn. Only stamped when there is a change.

hint.description: A short line under the value: Since last month.

icon.description: A system icon name or a node at the end of the label line. Decorative, hidden from assistive tech.

size.description: The size of the value: font.size 2xl, 4xl and 6xl.

loading.description: Draws a placeholder block for the value, sets aria-busy and data-loading, hides the change.

loadingLabel.description: What screen readers hear while loading. جار التحميل under an Arabic Theme.

trendLabels.description: Overrides the trend words: { up, down, flat }. Default Up, Down, No change, or ارتفاع، انخفاض، بدون تغيير.

a11y.focus: Never focusable.
a11y.announce: The change is read with its trend word first: Up 12%. Value changes are not announced, so a page of refreshing KPIs stays quiet. While loading, aria-busy is set and the value says loadingLabel.

data-trend on the root carries up, down or flat. It is a valued attribute, so it is listed here and under props, not under states, until the contract suite knows valued states.
Numbers use tabular figures, so a refreshing value does not shift its neighbours.
Under forced colors the loading block keeps a CanvasText border.
The trend icons (trend-up, trend-down) do not mirror in right to left layouts, like chart glyphs; the trend word carries the meaning.

A row in a list or table that needs its state at a glance, with the words in the label
A state that is going on now, such as syncing or recording, with pulse
avoidWhen: The state is the only thing on the line and needs a filled shape to read as a tag
A count of unread or new items
A message that explains what happened or what to do
The dot would be the only sign of the state, with no words anywhere

label.description: The state in words. Always rendered: visible, or visually hidden with hideLabel.

tone.description: The dot color, from the state border tokens (3:1 against body, surface and surface-2). accent takes color.primary.border.

pulse.description: A ring grows from the dot and fades, three times, then stops (under five seconds, WCAG 2.2.2). Only for a live state. Sets data-pulse.

hideLabel.description: Hides the label visually and keeps it for screen readers. Only where visible text nearby already names the same state, such as a group heading Online now; otherwise the dot would be color alone. Sets data-hide-label.

a11y.focus: Not focusable.
a11y.announce: Not announced. The label is read in reading order. A consumer that changes the state live and needs it read puts role status on the root or on a parent.
notes: Never color alone (WCAG 1.4.1): the label is required.
The dot is a non text mark at 3:1 against the surfaces it sits on (WCAG 1.4.11).
The pulse plays three times and stops; it does not restart on a re-render. The label carries the live state after that.

en.label: One to three words, sentence case, the state not the color: Online, Sync failed, Waiting for review.

ar.label: Noun or adjective forms, no diacritics: متصل، فشل المزامنة، في الانتظار.

name: Surface
summary: A plain background box on one surface step (body, surface 1 to 5), with an optional border, elevation, radius and padding.
useWhen: A region needs its own background step to separate it from the page, such as a sidebar fill or a summary box
Building a larger component (a tile, a panel body) that should take its fill from the surface tokens
Nesting boxes so each one sits one surface step above its parent
avoidWhen: The whole box is clickable or selectable
The box has a title, media and actions in a fixed layout
Only space is needed, with no fill or edge
A floating layer above the page, such as a menu or a popover

level.description: The surface step: body is color.bg.body, 1 is color.bg.surface, 2 to 5 are color.bg.surface-2 to -5. React takes the numbers 1 to 5 or the same digits as strings. Stamped as data-level.

bordered.description: A 1px border in color.border.default. Stamped as data-bordered.

elevation.description: Shadow from elevation.card or elevation.panel. Stamped as data-elevation.

radius.description: A radius token name. Stamped as data-radius. No pill: a block box would clip its text into the round ends.

padding.description: Inner space on every side, a space token step. Stamped as data-padding.

as.description: The element. Pick the one that says what the box is.

a11y.role: No role of its own: the native role of the element given by as (a div by default, no role). A section or aside with an accessible name becomes a landmark.
a11y.focus: Not focusable. Controls inside keep their own order.
a11y.announce: Nothing of its own. The content is read in document order.
notes: Text inside reads color.text.default, which the contrast gate checks against every surface step. Muted, dim and subtle text are checked only up to surface 3 (subtle up to surface 2): on levels 4 and 5 use default or bright text.

The border is always 1px and transparent at rest, so in forced colors mode the system draws it and the box keeps an edge without its fill or shadow. The cost: padding none still insets the content by that 1px.

en.body: Any content. The surface adds no copy of its own.

ar.body: Any content. The surface mirrors with the page through logical properties.

angular.note: Stamps the same data attributes; Surface.css is used as is.

native.note: Elevation maps to the platform shadow or Android elevation.

styles.desk: The same steps on the black desk. Elevation reads the deep Desk shadows.
styles.neutral: White and soft gray steps, light first. Small soft shadows for elevation.

name: Theme
summary: Stamps every runtime axis on its own element, resolves what is not passed from the nearest parent Theme, and gives the subtree its direction, icon set and style data.
useWhen: At the root of an app, once, so tokens, base CSS, direction and icons apply
Around a subtree that needs another scheme, style, density, language or direction
Around a demo or a preview that shows one combination of axes
avoidWhen: Changing one color or size in one place: use a component prop or a token
Setting dir or lang alone on an element: the tokens, Radix and the icons would not follow
Wrapping every component: one Theme per subtree that changes an axis is enough

style.description: The style pack id. Any custom id is accepted. At the root the default is studio; nested, the parent's.

scheme.description: Default from the style.json at the root, the parent's when nested. A scheme the style does not list falls back to its default.

density.description: Default from the style.json at the root, the parent's when nested.

glass.description: Read only by styles that use glass.

dir.description: Follows lang when lang is passed and dir is not. Otherwise the parent's, then from lang.

lang.description: A BCP 47 tag. The system ships en and ar.

css.description: Inline styles for the Theme element, as a React style object. style is taken by the style axis.

a11y.focus: Never focusable. It adds no role.
notes: dir and lang on the element let screen readers pick the right voice and let CSS mirror the layout.
The Radix direction provider follows dir, so menus, sliders and arrow keys mirror in right to left.
Arabic text gets IBM Plex Sans Arabic, zero tracking, taller lines and small text one step up through base.css. Body text keeps its size.

A root Theme is needed even when <html> is stamped with themeAttributes(): attributes give the CSS its axes but no React context, so useTheme, useOptionalPart and the Dialog and Toaster portals would fall back to the root defaults (Studio dark, English). Stamp <html> for the first paint and wrap the app in <Theme> with the same axes.

en.lang: Set lang on the root Theme. A Latin island inside Arabic is any element with lang en; it gets the Latin type back.

ar.lang: Set lang ar on the root Theme. dir follows as rtl.

react.note: Exports Theme, useTheme, useOptionalPart, themeAttributes and resolveTheme from packages/react/src/theme. themeAttributes() on <html> does not replace the root <Theme>: attributes carry no React context.

angular.note: dsTheme directive in packages/angular/src/theme, inputs named like the React props. A static style="desk" never reaches the style input (the Angular compiler parses it as inline CSS): bind [style]="'desk'" or use dsTheme="desk". Inline styles pass through css. Provides DsThemeService (value signal, optionalPart), the CDK Directionality and the icon style to its subtree. applyDocumentTheme stamps the html element.

native.note: ThemeProvider passes the resolved theme object through context, with the same axis names.

styles.studio: Black body, Inter Variable, default density
styles.desk: Black desk, Instrument Sans, default density, window and dialog controls and titlebar turned on

useWhen: A browsable grid of files, boards, templates or assets, where the thumbnail and the name do most of the work
A Studio dashboard of many equal items that should read as one surface cut into cells
A grid where every item opens on click and holds at most one or two icon actions
avoidWhen: An item that needs a description, a body or labelled buttons
A single item on its own, away from a grid
Rows of text that people scan and compare
Picking one option out of several

size.description: Padding and type size: space s with a small title, or space l with a medium title.

selected.description: Draws a 2px ring inside the tile (not color alone) and sets data-selected. Say it in words too, with aria-current on the TileLink.

asChild.description: On Tile and TileGrid: renders the single child element as the root, for example a ul grid of li tiles.

href.description: On TileLink: the target. Its hit area covers the whole tile.

children.description: TileMedia, TileTitle (with a TileLink), TileMeta, TileActions. TileGrid takes Tiles.

a11y.role: None on the tile. The title is a heading; a whole tile link is one native link inside it. A ul TileGrid with li tiles (asChild) gives a list role and a count.
a11y.focus: The tile never takes focus. Tab reaches the TileLink, then the actions. Focus draws a double ring inside the tile (2px ring, 2px gap, 2px ring), so the grid's clip never hides it and it never looks like the single selected ring.

keys.Tab: Moves to the tile link, then to its actions, then to the next tile
keys.Enter: On the tile link: opens it

notes: The title is cut at two lines with an ellipsis; the link still holds the full name. Keep names short enough to read in two lines.
Actions sit above the stretched link target and keep their own 24px targets.
Forced colors: every tile gets a CanvasText border, the selected one a Highlight outline at its edge, focus a Highlight outline one step further in.

name: TitleBar
summary: The bar at the top of a window or a panel: window controls at the start, the title, then trailing actions.
useWhen: The header of a Window, or of a Dialog drawn as a window in Desk
A panel header that needs a title and a close button
avoidWhen: The header of a page
A toolbar of many tools with no title

title.description: The title. One line with an ellipsis.

titleId.description: id of the title, for aria-labelledby on the window or dialog.

actions.description: The end slot: IconButtons and small Buttons.

moveLabel.description: Puts the title in a focusable move handle (part move, role group) named by this label: "Move window". The host (Window) listens for the keys there.

moveHint.default: Arrow keys move the window. Shift moves it further.
moveHint.description: Description of the move handle, through aria-describedby. Under lang="ar" the default is مفاتيح الأسهم لتحريك النافذة، ومع Shift لمسافة أبعد.

a11y.role: none: a plain container. The title is a heading (h2 by default).
a11y.focus: The bar itself is not focusable. With moveLabel the move handle is a tab stop with the 2px ring; while it has keyboard focus the title wraps to show in full. Then the controls and actions take focus in order.

keys.Tab: Moves through the controls, the move handle and the actions

Parts minimize, zoom and close are IconButtons a host renders in the actions slot when it has no lights (Window in Studio). They belong to the TitleBar, their nearest root.
In right to left layouts a bar with controls keeps them at the top left and centers the title, as macOS draws it. A bar without controls mirrors.

en.title: A file or app name in sentence case.

ar.title: Noun form, no diacritics. Latin file names go through Bidi.

styles.desk: Transparent, as the source .dwin-bar: the window glass shows through, no divider. The lights sit at the start.

mistakes.right: The full text stays in the title; a Tooltip shows it

name: Toast
summary: A short notice that something happened, shown in a corner and gone on its own. Called from anywhere with toast(); one Toaster renders them. Call shape: toast(title, options) or toast(options); toast.success, toast.warning, toast.danger and toast.info set the tone; each returns the id; toast.dismiss(id) closes one (or all, without an id), toast.update(id, patch) changes one in place, toast.configure(config) sets the max and the durations for the app.
useWhen: Confirming that an action the person took has finished: Draft saved, Link copied
A failure the person can fix later or retry from the toast, as tone danger with one action
A background event worth knowing now: a new version, a finished upload
Progress that ends in a result, updated in place with toast.update
avoidWhen: The person needs to make a decision before going on
Long content, a list, or anything to read twice
A critical error that blocks the task or loses data
A message tied to one field or one place on the page
Something that must stay on screen while the condition lasts

parts.Toast: root, without behavior and without data-state
parts.isInsideToaster: helper for overlays: true for a target inside the toaster

tone.description: The color and icon, and the timing: neutral, info and success close after 4s, warning after 6s, danger stays until closed.

title.description: One line: what happened, naming the thing.

description.description: More detail. Long text wraps in full; keep it to one or two sentences.

duration.description: toast() option. Milliseconds before it closes; Infinity keeps it. Default by tone. Ignored for danger and for a toast with an action, which stay until closed. toast.configure({ durations, max }) lengthens them for the whole app.

action.description: toast() option. One button: { label, onAction, altText }. A toast with an action never times out. altText is read in place of the button, for example where else the same action lives.

dedupeKey.description: toast() option. A toast that reads the same as an open one bumps its count instead of stacking; a key groups repeats with other copy; false turns it off.

id.description: toast() option. A call with the id of an open toast updates it.

lang.description: toast() option. The language of the copy when it differs from the page. The root gets lang and dir.

count.description: Toast prop. The repeat count; the Toaster passes it from the store.

onClose.description: Toast prop. Renders the close button and is called by it. The Toaster always renders it.

closeLabel.description: The accessible name of the close button. Arabic under lang ar.

position.description: Toaster prop. end is the inline end: right in English, left in Arabic.

label.description: Toaster prop. The name of the region. {hotkey} in it is replaced by the hotkey.

hotkey.description: Toaster prop. The keys that move focus to the toasts.

store.description: Toaster prop. The store to render. Default the app wide store behind toast().

a11y.role: The Toaster is a region (named Notifications) holding a list; each toast is a list item. Announcements go through two visually hidden regions owned by the Toaster: role status (polite) and role alert (assertive, for danger).
a11y.focus: Not modal: toasts never take focus on their own. F8 moves focus to the list, which shows the focus ring; Tab moves through the toasts, newest first, and each toast's action and close button. Closing the focused toast puts focus on the list. While a dialog with a focus trap is open, keyboard focus stays in the dialog: the toasts stay visible, readable and clickable, and a toast with an action waits until the dialog closes.

keys.F8: Moves focus to the notifications list
keys.Tab: Moves to the next toast, action or close button
keys.Enter: Runs the focused action or close button
keys.Escape: Closes a toast only when the key comes from inside the toaster: the focused toast, or the newest one from the list. Escape anywhere else, in a Window, a Dialog or a form, leaves every toast alone, a danger toast included, and is not prevented, so the system Dialog still closes itself. A raw Radix Dialog from a consumer does not get that Escape while a toast shows above it (Radix gives Escape to the top layer only), so use the system Dialog or close the toast first.

a11y.announce: Once per change (WCAG 4.1.3): when a toast shows, and again on each repeat or update, as "Notification. Title. Description. Action alternative." with the toast's text in the toast's language. danger is assertive (role alert), the rest polite (role status). The toast itself has no live role and keeps its element across a repeat or update, so it is never read twice and focus stays. Radix's own announcer is muted. The close button is not read.
notes: danger toasts and toasts with an action stay until closed. The others pause while the pointer is over them, while focus is inside, and while the window is blurred or the tab hidden (WCAG 2.2.1). toast.configure({ durations }) lengthens them for the whole app.
Swipe toward the edge closes a toast; the close button is the button path for the same action (WCAG 2.5.7).

Above an open modal dialog the toasts stay visible (z.toast is above z.dialog), stay in the accessibility tree and take the pointer. A dialog calls isInsideToaster(event.target) in onFocusOutside, onPointerDownOutside and onInteractOutside and prevents the default, so a toast never closes it.
At most three toasts show at once; the rest wait their turn, so a burst never covers the page.
No native title attribute anywhere.

en.title: Say what happened and name the thing: Draft saved, Could not upload photo.jpg. Sentence case, no exclamation marks.
en.description: Optional. What it means or what to do next, in one or two short sentences. Long text wraps in full, so keep it short.
en.action: A verb plus a noun: Retry upload, Undo move, Open draft. Never OK, Continue, Confirm or Yes. One action at most. The toast then stays until closed.
en.danger: Name the failure and what is safe: Could not publish page. Your draft is safe.
en.repeats: Keep the copy the same for the same event, so repeats fold into one toast with a count.

name: Window
summary: An app window over the page: a title bar, a body and an optional footer. It opens from a trigger, moves, zooms, minimizes and closes. Desk draws it as a glass window with traffic lights; Studio as a flat panel with a close button.
useWhen: A tool or a document the person works in next to the page: a board, a file browser, settings
Several views the person arranges side by side and brings to the front
Content that opens from a control and should grow out of it
avoidWhen: A decision that blocks the page until it is made
A short message with no work in it
A list of actions behind one control
Content that belongs in the page flow

parts.WindowLayer: none: the positioned layer that hosts windows (data-ds window-layer, a region named Windows, النوافذ in Arabic). Not a part of a window; see a11y notes

kind.description: Sets data-kind. canvas: a large window with a margin of layer around it, no body padding. finder: wide, the layer edge around it. settings: centered, as tall as its content.

title.description: Names the window through aria-labelledby. One line with an ellipsis.

actions.description: IconButtons or small Buttons at the end of the title bar, before the window buttons. They are TitleBar parts.

footer.description: The footer part, for the window's Buttons.

open.description: Controlled open state, with onOpenChange. Keep rendering the Window with open={false}: it stays mounted while window-close plays, then renders nothing. Unmounting it instead (a conditional render) skips the close motion.

zoomed.description: Fills the layer. Sets data-zoomed and aria-pressed on the zoom light.

onZoomedChange.description: With it, or inside a WindowLayer, zoom works: the zoom light (Desk), the zoom IconButton (Studio), Enter on the move handle and a double click on the title bar.

minimized.description: Plays window-minimize toward the dock, then hides the window. Sets data-minimized.

onMinimizedChange.description: With it minimize works: the minimize light (Desk) or IconButton (Studio). The app shows the way back (a dock) and sets minimized to false.

frame.description: { x, y, width, height } in px: x from the inline start edge of the layer, y from the top. null lets the kind place the window. Controlled with onFrameChange.

onFrameChange.description: Called on every move by key or pointer, with the clamped frame.

movable.description: Drag by the title bar and move with the arrow keys. Default true inside a WindowLayer or with a frame. A Window outside a WindowLayer sits in the page flow (position relative), has no frame and does not move unless it gets a frame.

origin.description: An element, a ref or a screen rect the window grows out of and closes back into. Focus returns to it on close.

dock.description: An element, a ref or a screen rect a minimized window falls into. Default the bottom center of the layer. Focus goes to it when nothing before it in the focus order can take focus.

modal.description: aria-modal and a Tab loop inside the window. Off by default: windows sit next to the page.

closeLabel.description: Under lang="ar" the default is إغلاق النافذة. A prop always wins.

minimizeLabel.description: Under lang="ar" the default is تصغير النافذة. A prop always wins.

zoomLabel.description: Under lang="ar" the default is تكبير النافذة. A prop always wins.

controlsLabel.description: Under lang="ar" the default is أزرار النافذة. A prop always wins.

moveLabel.description: Name of the move handle: the title of a window that can move, focusable, a TitleBar part. Under lang="ar" the default is تحريك النافذة.

moveHint.description: Description of the move handle. Default names the arrow keys, Shift, and Enter when zoom works, in Arabic under lang="ar".

a11y.role: dialog, named by the title (aria-labelledby) or aria-label. Not modal unless modal is set.
a11y.focus: Focus moves into the window (the window element, tabindex -1) when it opens after mount, or on mount when its origin has focus. When the window closes or minimizes, focus goes to the first of: the origin, the next active window of the layer, the element that had focus before it opened, the dock, the WindowLayer (a region with tabindex -1). It moves only when focus was in the window or lost. Keyboard focus and pointer down both bring a window to the front.

keys.Escape: Closes the window. A control inside that handles Escape itself (a menu) prevents it first.
keys.ArrowUp: Moves the window up 16px, while focus is on the window or on its move handle (the title)
keys.ArrowDown: Moves the window down 16px, from the same places
keys.ArrowLeft: Moves the window 16px to the left on screen, in both directions
keys.ArrowRight: Moves the window 16px to the right on screen, in both directions
keys.Shift+ArrowUp, Shift+ArrowDown, Shift+Ar: Moves the window 64px, from the same places
keys.Enter: On the move handle: zooms the window or puts it back, when zoom works
keys.Tab: Moves through the lights or the title bar buttons, the move handle, the title bar actions, the body and the footer. With modal, Tab stays inside the window.

a11y.announce: The title is the accessible name of the dialog. The lights and the close button carry their own labels.
notes: Every drag has a key path (WCAG 2.1.1, 2.5.7): the arrow keys move the window from the window element or the move handle. The frame is clamped so 160px of the window and its title bar stay inside the layer.
Arrow keys pressed on a light, an action or anything in the body never move the window, so a roving toolbar in actions keeps its arrows.
Zoom has a key and a button in every style: Enter on the move handle, the zoom light in Desk, the zoom IconButton in Studio. A double click on the title bar is a pointer shortcut for the same action.
Moving is off while the window is zoomed, and for a window placed by its parent with no frame. The move handle is rendered only while the window can move.
Tab order follows the DOM order of the windows, not their stacking. Moving focus into a window with Tab brings it to the front.
A long title truncates with an ellipsis; the full text is the accessible name, and keyboard focus on the move handle wraps the title to show it in full.
No native title attribute.

WindowLayer is the container for windows, not a part of one: a positioned region (tabindex -1, named Windows) that stacks its windows, tracks the active one through the shared window manager and takes focus when its last window leaves. useWindowLayer() returns that manager, for a dock that restores minimized windows.

A Window outside a WindowLayer sits in the page flow (position relative), takes the size its parent gives it, has no frame and does not move. Give it a frame (and a positioned parent) to place and move it.
The five chrome labels (close, minimize, zoom, the controls group, the move handle) and the move hint default to Arabic under lang="ar", as Dialog and Toast do. A prop always wins.
Contract suite (many case, focus on the move handle): the arrow keys are checked with moves, Shift with the arrows with moves further, Escape with closes and Enter (zoom) with state-changes.

Arrow keys move the window in the physical direction on screen, in both directions: ArrowRight moves it right in Arabic too. A window is a spatial object on a desk, like a dragged card; a text or list control follows the reading direction, a positioned object does not (lead decision, wave 1).
Enter on the move handle zooms, and the handle is not rendered while the window is zoomed: focus moves to the window element (WCAG 2.4.3) and back to the handle when the window is restored.

name: WindowControls
summary: The traffic lights of a window: close, minimize and zoom. 12px lights with 24 by 24 px targets, each an IconButton with its own label.
useWhen: The controls slot of a TitleBar in a style that turns the window controls part on (Desk)
A window picture where the lights are shown but do nothing, with no handlers
avoidWhen: A panel in a style without lights (Studio)
Any control that is not close, minimize or zoom of a window

onClose.description: Without it the close light is disabled.

closeDisabled.description: With onClose: the close light is aria-disabled and data-disabled, stays in the tab order, blocks activation and draws as an idle dot; its glyph still shows on hover and focus. For a window or dialog that cannot be dismissed right now.

onMinimize.description: Without it the minimize light is disabled.

onZoom.description: Without it the zoom light is disabled.

closeLabel.description: Under lang="ar" the default is إغلاق النافذة. A prop always wins.

minimizeLabel.description: Under lang="ar" the default is تصغير النافذة. A prop always wins.

zoomLabel.description: Under lang="ar" the default is تكبير النافذة. A prop always wins.

label.description: The name of the group. Under lang="ar" the default is أزرار النافذة. A prop always wins.

active.description: data-state active or inactive, for hosts and recipes. As in the source, it does not change how the lights look.

a11y.role: group, named by label. Each light is a native button (IconButton).
a11y.focus: Each light with a handler is in the tab order with the 2px ring around its 24px target. A light with no handler is aria-disabled and out of the tab order (tabIndex -1): an accepted exception to the rule that disabled actions stay focusable, because a dead light is inert decoration of the window chrome; a screen reader still finds it, dimmed. A close light disabled through closeDisabled is an action that cannot run now: it stays focusable with aria-disabled, like any disabled Button.

keys.Enter: Presses the focused light. Nothing happens on a disabled light.
keys.Tab: Moves to the next light with a handler

a11y.announce: Each light is named by its label. The zoom light reports pressed while the window is zoomed.
notes: Never color alone: the glyphs (x, minus, arrows) show with the colors on hover and on keyboard focus of the group, and always in forced colors.
The lights do not mirror in right to left layouts. They keep the order close, minimize, zoom from the left, as macOS draws them and as the source does.
Targets are 24 by 24 px and touch, so light centers are 24px apart (WCAG 2.5.8).
No native title attribute.
